Sports.title: Ian Wright hits out at 'ridiculous and poor' World Cup final pitch at the MetLife Stadium - and that was BEFORE extravagant half-time show featuring Justin Bieber and Shakira
Sports.content:
Ian Wright has hit out at the state of the World Cup final pitch, dubbing it 'ridiculous, bobbly and poor'.

The MetLife Stadium has been criticised throughout this summer's tournament and once again appeared dry and patchy as Spain took on Argentina tonight.

A number of instances saw stars, including the great Lionel Messi, struggle to control the ball as it bobbled along the uneven surface.

And speaking during ITV's half-time coverage of the clash, Wright didn't hold any punches while assessing the venue for the biggest game in the footballing calendar.

He said: 'For a World Cup final this pitch is ridiculous, it's poor, it (the game) shouldn't be on it.

'I think Spain are playing and showing how good they are because even on a bobbly, dry pitch like this, they're doing really good stuff.

Ian Wright has hit out at the state of the World Cup final pitch, dubbing it 'ridiculous, bobbly and poor'

The turf in New Jersey has come in for criticism throughout the tournament

'I think Argentina will stay in it but, for me, Spain are passing it all over the place. It's only a matter of time before they take one of these chances.'

The 80,000-capacity MetLife sits on the outskirts of New York, which was hit by severe thunderstorms causing flooding in the hours ahead of kick-off in the sweltering east coast sunshine.

Yet the pitch had been deemed subpar by players and managers long before it was hit by rainfall.

It predominantly consists of natural grass, but the turf has been installed over an artificial surface underneath which can make it 'dry out' quickly when temperatures soar.

Brazil star Vinicius Jr was one of the stars who took issue with the surface earlier in the tournament, telling reporters after his country's 1-1 draw with Morocco: 'Because of the weather and the heat, the grass dries out quickly and the game ends up being very slow.

'We can't build up a rhythm. That makes things difficult because we want to move the ball from one side to the other and this disrupts our game.'

French coach Didier Deschamps later criticised the venue, saying: 'The pitch in New York was really tough - it took a lot out of the players' muscles.'

Wright's comments came moments before the broadcaster's coverage cut to the highly-anticipated half-time show, which was facilitated by a controversial interval of 30 minutes.

A star-studded half-time show featured performances from Shakira (pictured) and Justin Bieber

It featured a star-studded lineup including performances by Shakira, Burna Boy, Justin Bieber and Madonna - and even cameo appearances from footballing royalty Ronaldinho and Ronaldo.

Madonna kickstarted the performance with her hit 'Music', walking out onto the field with 2002 World Cup winners and Brazilian legends Ronaldo and Ronaldinho.

Bieber was then introduced by Ted Lasso for a short, slow acoustic performance while a montage of the tournament was playing on the big screens around the 80,000-seater stadium.

Shakira later returned and injected some energy into the show before the performance came to an end and the preparation for the second half quickly restarted.

Yet ITV's panel of pundits were left less than impressed by the show - as was Wayne Rooney on the BBC.

Keane said: 'A bit of anti-climax but I think the people in the stadium probably enjoyed it more than us. It was nice to see Shakira.'

Wright added: '(Justin) Bieber should have done something a bit more upbeat to liven us up a bit.'

While Rooney reflected bluntly: 'My favourite bit of the half time show was when it finished… I like all of them artists but I thought it was crap.'

A host of stars flooded to New Jersey for the climax of this summer's tournament.

Before kick-off, Top Gun and Mission Impossible superstar Tom Cruise took to the pitch to give a motivational pre-match speech. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump was pictured sat in his luxury suite next to FIFA President Gianni Infantino.

Celebrity couple Timothee Chalament and Kylie Jenner were also snapped in the stands, as were Mick Jagger, Pharrell Williams, Victoria Beckham and Will Ferrell.

Despite the substandard quality of the surface, Spain ultimate ran out victorious on the east coast thanks to a late goal from Ferran Torres.

After a ball was swung in from the right, Nico Williams nodded a header down from the far post, which the Barcelona striker latched on to and fired into the roof of the net to spark jubilant scenes.

The South Americans applied pressure of their own in search of a goal late on and Tottenham Hotspur defender Marcos Senesi almost levelled from close range.

But, in the end, it wasn't to be for Lionel Messi on what could his final appearance on football's biggest stage as Lamine Yamal and his Spanish team-mates held on for a historic victory.

Joe Hart said on the BBC: 'They were never rattled or under pressure. They haven't nibbled once. They played beautiful football the entire time.

'Yamal, at 19 years old, his confidence, the ways that he's doing this. Everyone will be trying to get on his back and hate on him, but he's got a Euros and World Cup. He kept so cool, kept his head, and had those standout moments.'

The match was, however, at times overshadowed by the antics of the Argentinians.

After taunting England's stars in Atlanta on Wednesday, Argentina's behaviour against Spain was dubbed 'embarrassing by pundits' after the final whistle in New Jersey.

Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez saw red in the 90+3-minute for a late challenge on Pau Cabarsi before chaotic scenes were sparked on the pitch when Spain's win was confirmed.

As the Spanish bench descended onto the pitch to celebrate, Argentinian substitute Leandro Paredes took issue with Barcelona midfielder Gavi.

The pair became embroiled in a row, causing Scaloni to intervene, before Paredes appeared to direct two punches at Gavi as he fell to the turf.

And, speaking on the BBC, ex-Man United striker Wayne Rooney was scathing in his criticism of Argentina's behaviour not only on Sunday, but throughout the tournament.

He said: 'It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this from Argentina before. It's just sad, very poor from them. If you lose a game of football, be graceful. It's a reaction to them being outplayed. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves it's well.'

How much is David Beckham set to pocket from his World Cup brand deals? Take on our quiz in our newsletter HERE.

Sports.title: Donald Trump ignores FIFA president's call to leave the stage as he joins Spain's World Cup final trophy lift in awkward moment
Sports.content:
US President Donald Trump took center stage at MetLife Stadium on Sunday to hand the FIFA World Cup trophy to Spain's triumphant stars after their dramatic final win.

The European outfit clinched their second World Cup title after beating Lionel Messi's Argentina 1-0 in extra time, following a late strike from forward Ferran Torres.

Shortly after the full-time whistle, the US President made his way down to the field and onto a stage which had been constructed, along with FIFA chief Gianni Infantino.

Trump and Infantino handed out various awards to match officials and players, before officially welcoming Spain's players up to the stage to lift the World Cup trophy.

The US President presented the prestigious title to Spain captain and Manchester City midfielder Rodri, who took great pleasure in raising it aloft in East Rutherford.

Much like when he presented the Club World Cup title last summer, Trump stood awkwardly alongside the Spain squad as they raised the trophy and celebrated wildly.

Donald Trump took center stage as Spain lifted the World Cup trophy on Sunday afternoon

The President, along with FIFA chief Gianni Infantino, presented the award to Spain

It appeared as though Infantino attempted to usher Trump away - but the President remained

It seemed as though, when Spain were about to do the trophy lift, that Infantino had attempted to usher Trump away from the players - though the President remained.

He stood to the side of the squad as the confetti cannons went off at MetLife Stadium, clapping and grinning while Infantino laughed off Trump's awkward cameo.

There were an estimated 1.5-1.8 billion viewers who tuned in to watch the summer tournament's showpiece finale, where Trump and Infantino took center stage.

There were also loud boos coming from the stands when Infantino and Trump made their way onto the pitch, as fans made their feelings on the duo undoubtedly clear.

Prior to the official trophy lift, Trump also handed out silver medals to Argentina's players - including Lionel Messi - after their heartbreaking defeat in New Jersey.

Fans noted that one Argentina star - Tottenham defender Cristian Romero - completely ignored the President as he collected his medal from Infantino.

In a video which swiftly went viral on social media, the Argentinian could be seen receiving his silverware from the FIFA chief before waltzing past Trump on stage.

Meanwhile, Trump also presented a trio of awards to Spain's stars; including the Young Player of the Tournament, the Golden Glove and the Golden Ball - which were claimed by Pau Cubarsi, Unai Simon and Rodri respectively.

The US President welcomed Spain's stars onto the stage before presenting the prestigious title

The President also handed out silver medals to Lionel Messi and Argentina after their loss

Trump pictured presenting Lamine Yamal with his medal after the 1-0 win at MetLife Stadium

Argentina defender Cristian Romero appeared to ignore Trump as he walked on stage

There was a degree of irony in regards to Trump presenting Spain with the World Cup trophy, after previously launching a stinging attack on the country at a UN summit earlier in July for not contributing enough money to NATO.

'Spain is a terrible partner in NATO. They don’t participate. They don’t pay. I don’t want anything to do with Spain. Cut off all trade with Spain, please, including visits,' he said. 'Don’t even talk to them. They’re hopeless, bad people.'

Then, on his way back to the United States on Air Force One, Trump said Spain had tried to improve their standings with him.

'I did have issues, and ​I still do. But Spain, they came back all the way today. Spain was very generous today,' he said.

'They honoured a request for lots of payments, and if they didn't, we wouldn't have even ⁠talked to them.'

Earlier in the day, Trump and his wife Melania were seen taking in the action inside a packed MetLife Stadium suite - alongside FIFA President Infantino, Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney and Mexico's President Claudia Sheinbaum.

Trump also shook hands with Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez as Infantino stood beside them.

Spain's Queen Letizia and King Felipe VI also greeted the president. Javier Milei, the president of Argentina, is watching the game from home due to 'superstition,' The New York Times reported.

Trump cozied up to FIFA President Gianni Infantino in the private suite on Sunday afternoon in New Jersey

Inside the private suite, Infantino posed for pictures with the president's son, Eric Trump, his wife, Lara, and their children

President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania joined the massive crowd at MetLife Stadium on Sunday afternoon for the 2026 World Cup final match

The commander-in-chief also waved at the crowd from behind the glass.

Inside the private suite, Infantino posed for pictures with the president's son, Eric Trump, his wife, Lara, and their children. Barron Trump also showed up for the big game.

Ahead of the match, Trump told Fox News' Jenny Taft on the FIFA Red Carpet that 'it's hard to bet against Messi,' speaking of Argentina's 39-year-old star.

However, in the end, it wasn't to be for the veteran soccer star after he and Argentina came up short in their battle against European outfit Spain in East Rutherford.

The match was decided by a ferocious, close-range strike from Spanish star Ferran Torres in the 106th minute, after a 0-0 stalemate at the end of regulation time.

However, there were ugly scenes once the full-time whistle blew - with a number of frustrated Argentina stars taking out their anger on Spain's players.

After the whistle, Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes was sent off for punching Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground.

Argentina's Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso as he was running by, while Thiago Almada was involved, too.

Lionel Messi's bid for back-to-back World Cup titles ended in failure after their loss to Spain

Several stars clashed after Spain's 1-0 win as Argentina - but the South Americans started it

Argentina's Leandro Paredes was sent off after the whistle for getting violent with Spain

Micah Richards said of their behaviour on the BBC: 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time.

'Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest. Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Argentina only had two shots in the entire match, and the first of those only came in the 117th minute.

By contrast, they committed 24 fouls - though Spain didn't have clean hands themselves, as they gave away 21.

Sports.title: World Cup fans brand FIFA's first-ever halftime show a 'disaster' as Madonna and Bieber's bizarre spectacle divides billions
Sports.content:
Have you got a story? Email tips@dailymail.com

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

World Cup fans branded FIFA's controversial first-ever World Cup halftime show starring Madonna and Justin Bieber a 'disaster' on Sunday - as the spectacle divided viewers around the world.

Argentina and Spain superstars Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal were forced to share the stage on Sunday at MetLife Stadium as the Super Bowl-inspired performance got underway - before Spain triumphed 1-0 over Argentina in extra time.

The futuristic segment began with Madonna, 67, singing her 2000 hit Music, accompanied by giddy Brazilian World Cup legends Ronaldo Nazario and Ronaldinho.

The toned music legend was dressed head-to-toe in Saint Laurent, wowing in a pink satin teddy jacket and corset, mini shorts and lace-up boots, paired with stockings as she embraced the soccer icons, before they drove her out into the stadium.

The unlikely trio then posed up on the grass and smiled at the crowds.

Bieber, 32, made a starkly different impact on the crowd as he stepped out with nothing but a guitar to sing a World Cup themed version of his song, Everything Hallelujah.

The singer was bizarrely subbed onto the pitch by Jason Sudeikis, playing his manager alter-ego Ted Lasso.

Madonna and Justin Bieber's performances during the controversial first-ever FIFA World Cup halftime show divided fans on Sunday

Justin Bieber made a starkly different impact on the crowd as he stepped out with only a guitar to sing a World Cup-themed version of his song Everything Hallelujah - leaving fans baffled

Shakira showed off her toned frame as she performed her hit Dai Dai with Burna Boy

The star looked relaxed as he casually walked onto the pitch before belting out his hit track, adding the final line, 'it's the World Cup, Hallelujah' - with fans left baffled by his song choice.

One fan gave the damning verdict, 'What a disaster this halftime show was. Pre-recorded stuff, no collaborations or surprising moments. Where was Madonna at the end? She could have sung a few lines with Shakira... everything was so weird. So much hype for nothing.'

Yet making clear the division, a second viewer wrote, 'I dislike a lot of things that FIFA does... but THAT halftime show was pretty spectacular.'

Another wrote, 'Who was behind the concept for that haltfime show? Chat GPT?'

Other fans wrote, 'Madonna’s performance was the strangest thing ever, especially followed by the Muppets. The rest of the show was decent. I thought JB’s performance was the best of them all.'

'Light, bright, positive energy. We needed that. Really tired of dark and angry performances.

'It seemed like bieber was off the flow but when Shakira came up after - it all made sense!!!'

'It was great! International and diverse, a positive message, family friendly, and soccer legends hanging with Madonna! Ronaldinho and Ronaldo probably couldn't believe it!'

Bieber's downbeat song choice was undoubtedly one of the major talking points of the performance, with one fan writing, 'Justin Bieber was unfortunately the worst part of the World Cup halftime show.'

Another penned, 'Justin Bieber Hallelujah but this was not the right song choice for the half time show.'

A third typed, 'Buzz killer. Totally sucked . Why choose that song that nobody knows . Beyond me ….' while another wrote, 'terrible song choice.'

Others praised Bieber's performance, writing, 'Justin Bieber looked and sounded great at the World Cup halftime show today!

'Glad he's cleaned up his act!

'Best performance. He knows how to switch people’s moods in a second. That’s extremely difficult to do, most performers couldn’t.'

Shakira returned to the World Cup stage as she flaunted her toned abs in a pink and yellow sequined bodysuit to perform her hit Dai Dai, with Burna Boy, while K-pop sensations BTS regaled the crowd with Dynamite.

Spain eventually triumphed over Argentina 1-0 after a thrilling 30 minutes of extra time - seen with Trump at the trophy ceremony

The futuristic segment began with Madonna, 67, singing Music, accompanied by giddy World Cup legends Ronaldo Nazario and Ronaldinho

The toned music legend showed off her legs in stockings as she embraced the soccer icons, before they drove her out into the stadium

The trio posed up on the pitch as Madonna pulled off another flawless performance

The singer was bizarrely subbed onto the pitch by Jason Sudeikis playing manager Ted Lasso

Fans had vastly differing opinions on the show - one viewer branded the show 'spectacular'

Others blasted the show over pitchy vocals and lipsync allegations

Fans slammed Bieber for his song choice on sport's biggest stage

One fan branded Bieber the 'worst part' of the show

Others praised Bieber's performance as 'so good' and worthy of the Super Bowl

K-pop sensations BTS regaled the crowd with Dynamite

BTS captivated the crowds as they continued their return to the stage after military training

The show delivered a spectacular mix of music, nostalgia and global star power, including a cameo from The Muppets

The stadium was lit up with a colorful globe and the world LOVE

[IMG 320818273 noborder /] Fans had wildly differing opinions on the spectacular

Former England star Wayne Rooney savaged the controversial World Cup final halftime show, quipping the best part of it was 'when it finished'

Liam Gallagher savaged 'This is like a bad trip', before adding: 'It's a good job I've got my spiritual socks on or that halftime entertainment could have tipped me over the edge'

The show was also blasted by former World Cup England star Wayne Rooney, 41, who joked his favorite part of the show was 'when it finished'.

'To be honest mine was when it finished I like a lot of those artists but to be honest I thought it was c**p', he fumed.

'I did honestly. It just didn't get me going, I wanted the football to be back on. It was a bit flat. I like Burna Boy I like Shakira I like Bieber but that was too flat.'

Fans were left in hysterics by Rooney's comment, with one user on X laughing: 'Wayne Rooney on the halftime show actually made me LOL and then 'I like a lot of the artists, but I thought it was c**p'.

While Liam Gallagher savaged 'This is like a bad trip', before adding: 'It's a good job I've got my spiritual socks on or that halftime entertainment could have tipped me over the edge'.

As well as a halftime show, the World Cup final also included a closing ceremony that featured performances and appearances from Post Malone, Tom Cruise, Nicole Scherzinger, influencer IShowSpeed, Oscar winner Jennifer Hudson, Robbie Williams and Italian singer Laura Pausini.

Stars including Cruise, Timothee Chalamet, Kylie Jenner, Matt Damon and Adrien Brody joined the crowds for the final.

Spanish actor Javier Bardem, skiing legend Lindsey Vonn and actress Julia Garner were also in attendance for the FIFA Gold Carpet event ahead of the final.

Tom Cruise flashed a giddy grin as he sauntered through the stadium ahead of his special appearance at the closing ceremony

Matt Damon and Argentinian wife Luciana Barroso looked giddy as they arrived

Thousands of fans and media members faced massive lines to enter the stadium for the World Cup final on Sunday amid several reports of security struggling to manage the situation

Will Ferrell was in attendance for the huge match

Javier Bardem supported his home country as he walked the FIFA Gold Carpet before the final

Julia Garner was in attendance to support close pal Madonna ahead of her halftime show

Lindsey Vonn looked stylish as she posed up ahead of the game

Brazil legend Ronaldo Nazario attended with wife Celina Locks

England icon John Terry and Argentina legend Diego Simeone were in attendance

Spain triumphed over Messi's Argentina 1-0 - after a fraught second half which saw the teams play into 30 mins of extra time.

Ferran Torres netted the winning goal in the 106th minute - with a devastated Messi watching on as his World Cup career ended in heartbreak.

World Cup final day got off to a chaotic start at MetLife Stadium with fans forced to wait for hours outside of the venue amid reports of technological glitches scanning tickets and security staff unsure of how to manage the crowds.

The attendance of President Donald Trump meant that airport-style security measures were also being enforced for everyone making their way inside of the venue.

The game was set to be the most expensive to attend in the history of sport - on Sunday morning, the cheapest ticket available on most resale websites was starting at around $7,000.

FIFA encouraged fans to arrive early in order to participate in the World Cup closing ceremony, scheduled to begin around 90 minutes before the game itself kicks off.

But it is standard procedure for fans to arrive early for additional security checks whenever Trump attends a sporting event - and he has made it to plenty in his second term as President, ranging from the Ryder Cup to the Super Bowl.

Post Malone performed ahead of the final

Cruise kept his look casual in a black tee and jeans as he posed for selfies with queuing fans, while flanked by bodyguards

The star looked excited ahead of the final

Jon Hamm arrived at MetLife ahead of the ceremony

Robbie Williams, Nicole Scherzinger and Laura Pausini performed Desire

Extra security checks were in place ahead of the attendance of President Trump for the game

Man of the hour and Argentina captain Lionel Messi winked at fans as he arrived for the final - before his team heartbreakingly lost to Spain 1-0

Spain's Ferran Torres netted the winning goal in the 106th minute (top with Eric Garcia)

A devastated Messi was seen looking dejected after losing

Even on the live television coverage, the stadium was bare with a little over an hour until that closing ceremony began.

Soccer greats such as Brazil World Cup winner Ronaldo, former England captain John Terry and former Argentina player Diego Simeone all appeared carefree as they entered the stadium in good time before the game.

Argentina were narrow underdogs against Spain, the European champions, despite being the holders after winning the 2022 tournament in Qatar.

Sports.title: Spain 1-0 Argentina PLAYER RATINGS: Which two stars received 3/10 after dreadful displays? Who was 'imperious' but faded? And which Premier League stalwart delivered a 'shocking' first-half?
Sports.content:
Ferran Torres wrote his name into Spanish football history after scoring in the 106th minute of the World Cup final to break the hearts of Argentina and Lionel Messi.

The substitute, who smashed his finish into the roof of the net, reclaimed deserved glory for La Roja for the first time since 2010 after their opponents managed just two shots across the entirety of the match.

Spain's elegance and discipline was contrasted with the brutish skulduggery of Argentina, who saw Enzo Fernandez sent off in the 93rd minute. His midfield counterpart, Leandro Paredes, was also shown his marching orders after a violent clash after full-time.

Daily Mail Sport's CRAIG HOPE was at the MetLife Stadium to bring you our player ratings.

Spain have won the World Cup after a deserved 1-0 victory over Argentina on Sunday night

It was a devastating end for Lionel Messi though who has likely played his last World Cup game

Spain (4-2-3-1)

Unai Simon - 6

Twice off his line in a flash to clear after balls were dropped in behind for Messi and Alvarez to chase. But there was not a save to make.

Pedro Porro - 6

Hardly troubled in defence so took that opportunity to join attack, as he likes to. Heavily involved, - more than 120 touches - but crosses rarely found intended target.

Pau Cubarsi - 8

Tried to get his team going with forward passes from deep, including one to get Yamal away. Was super cool in defence, too. He’s a star.

Aymeric Laporte - 7

Rarely flustered at the back so subdued was Messi and thought he’d won it with late header plucked on goal-line by Martinez.

Marc Cucurella - 7

Typically snappy in his challenges and, like Porro, poured forward when realising how passive Argentina were. Nearly scored opener with low drill wide.

Rodri - 7

Imperious early on and everything went through him. He looked like the grown-up in midfield battle. That influence faded and he could not find the pass to break stubborn Argentina.

Rodri dictated the game for Spain in midfield and ended up winning Player of the Tournament

Pau Cubarsi was brilliant in defence and helped start Spain's attacks with his superb passing

Fabian Ruiz - 6

A threat amid otherwise mundane first half, but way below best. Came into it more after break and dribble led to good chance for Torres. Much like whole tournament, not the final we’d hoped for from him.

Lamine Yamal - 7

A threat amid otherwise mundane first half, but still below best. Came into it more after break and dribble led to good chance for Torres. Much like whole tournament, not really the final we’d hoped for from him, but played his part.

Dani Olmo - 6

Like many of Spain’s other attacking starters he just could not produce that moment of inspiration. Not as peripheral as the others, but no real impact.

Alex Baena - 4

No end product from left wing and was a surprise he stayed on until 75th minute. A big chance to impress but Atletico Madrid man did not take it.

Mikel Oyarzabal - 5

A star of the tournament but this was a game to forget on the biggest occasion. One shot on target and one touch in area before making way just after hour.

Mikel Oyarzabal has been one of the stars of the tournament but didn't enjoy his best game

Lamine Yamal was a threat throughout the match but the wonderkid was still below his best

Substitutes

Ferran Torres (on for Oyarzabal 62) - 8

Pedri (on for Fabian Ruiz 62) - 7

Mikel Merino (on for Olmo 75) - 6

Nico Williams (on for Baena 75) - 9

Martin Zubimendi (on for Rodri 99) - 6

Eric Garcia (on for Laporte 99) - 6

Manager: Luis de la Fuente - 8

Has now delivered the World Cup and European Championship. They made hard work of this and should have been good enough to win in normal time, but the introduction of Williams and Torres was the inspiration Spain needed.

Ferran Torres came off the bench to score Spain's winner and write himself into Spain's history

Argentina (4-4-2)

Emiliano Martinez - 8

Improvised early on to deny Yamal and that was the first of 11 saves. Kept his team in the game and had no chance with winner. Easily Argentina’s best.

Gonzalo Montiel - 6

Saved likely goal when stealing from toe of Cucurella in penalty area after half-time, but that was his last involvement. Had been solid before that.

Cristian Romero - 6

Never far from the action, as is his way, and got the better of Oyarzabal in duel with Spain’s five-goal striker. Seemed to tire after exertions of semi versus England.

Lisandro Martinez - 5

Injury nightmare just before half-time when hurting his thigh as he brought down Rodri. Long balls had been wasteful to that point.

Lisandro Martinez suffered an injury nightmare and was forced off before half-time

Emiliano Martinez kept his team in the game and ended up making 11 saves in total

Nicolas Tagliafico - 7

Tasked with keeping Yamal quiet and, one or two flashes from the Spain winger apart, it was a job he did well. Emerges with credit.

Rodrigo De Paul - 5

His loose pass caused team-mate Lisandro to foul Rodri at expense of booking and injury. Was diligent in defensive work but not good enough on the ball.

Alexis Mac Allister - 4

Shocking first half. Repeatedly found red with stray passes and was lucky to escape yellow for lunge on Olmo. Recovered to put in decent shift but quality still lacking.

Enzo Fernandez - 3

Red card shame on back of untidy display. He set the tone against England but was too passive here, except when committing the two second-half fouls that brought deserved yellows.

Nico Gonzalez - 3

Anonymous and invariably lost the ball when he did get it. Was no surprise to see him hooked at the break after completing only five passes.

Lionel Messi - 5

One touch first 15 minutes and that was from kick off. Also pulled out of 50-50 with Simon. Justin Bieber got closer to the penalty area in normal time. Belatedly came to life in final moments and was dangerous. All too late, though.

Lionel Messi was left heartbroken after enduring a quiet game as he struggled to get involved

Enzo Fernandez is the sixth player to be sent off during a World Cup final and let his side down

Julian Alvarez - 4

Tried to do the running while Messi walked but had no service and left the field after 102 minutes without a shot. You could sense his frustration.

Substitutes

Nicolas Otamendi (on for L Martinez 45) 6

Leandro Paredes (on for Gonzalez 46) 4

Nahuel Molina (on for Montiel 58) 5

Giuliano Simeone (on for De Paul 70) 5

Facundo Medina (on for Romero 70) 5

Marcos Senesi (on for Alvarez 102) 5

Manager: Lionel Scaloni - 4

Didn't send out his team with same snarliness as against England and, come the end, they had not even found the target over 120 minutes. A weak defence of their title.

Referee: Slavko Vincic - 5

Sports.title: World Cup final descends into violence at full-time whistle as Spain and Argentina players clash in ugly scenes
Sports.content:
The World Cup final descended into outrageous scenes as fights broke out among the two sets of players.

Some of Argentina's players lost their heads as Spain's substitutes and staff ran on to the pitch to celebrate their 1-0 win against the South Americans.

Ferran Torres scored a 106th-minute winner after Enzo Fernandez had been sent off in the 93rd minute for a desperately poor Argentina side.

After the whistle, Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes was sent off for punching Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground.

Argentina's Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso as he was running by, while Thiago Almada was involved, too.

Micah Richards said of their behaviour on the BBC: 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time.

'Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest. Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Argentina's Leandro Paredes was sent off after the whistle for getting violent with Spain

Several stars clashed after Spain's 1-0 win over Argentina - but the South Americans started it

Joe Hart added: 'Disgusting behaviour. There was one man on that pitch with class and that was Lionel Messi.'

Wayne Rooney said: 'It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this from Argentina before. It's just sad, very poor from them.

'If you lose a game of football, be graceful. It's a reaction to them being outplayed. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves.'

Argentina were thuggish throughout the World Cup final, just as they had been against England in the semis.

Fernandez complained against his dismissal for a second yellow but his late foul on Pau Cubarsi, which sent the defender flying, was atrocious.

Paredes was also fortunate to not be sent off in regular time for a foul on the edge of the box which presented Lamine Yamal with a last-breath free-kick before extra-time.

Argentina only had two shots in the entire match, and the first of those came in the 117th minute.

By contrast, they were trigger-happy on the fouls with 24 - though Spain didn't have clean hands themselves, as they gave away 21.

Paredes was blasted for getting violent at full time and trying to ruin Spain's celebrations

Alan Shearer said: 'There's a way to lose. Too many times we've seen that reaction from them. They were trying to win free-kicks and their reaction after full time was terrible. The best team won. It's a result for football because of the way Spain have played.'

Even Lionel Messi didn't rise above the dark arts. The legendary forward was lambasted by Wayne Rooney after he tried to get Marc Cucurella sent off during the latter stages of the game.

The game descended into chaos when Fernandez received his second yellow card.

This led to a melee between both sets of players and Cucurella was spotted saying something to Messi.

The left-back then put a couple of fingers over his mouth and continued speaking, a move which the Argentine immediately reacted to and waved over the referee.

As per FIFA's rules for this tournament, if a player holds their hand over their mouth in a confrontational situation, they will be sent off.

This was seen with Miguel Almiron for Paraguay in the group stage and Piero Hincapie in the knockout stages for Ecuador.

However, it didn't appear that Cucurella was speaking in a confrontational manner and the referee, nor VAR, decided to intervene.

Spain have won the World Cup after Ferran Torres' extra-time winner against Argentina

Torres smashed in the goal with his left foot after Williams headed the ball back across goal

It was elation for the Spanish players as they celebrated wildly in the corner of the stadium

But it was devastation for Argentina's crestfallen stars, who had fought for their lives

There was no fairytale World Cup ending for Lionel Messi who struggled to assert his authority

The BBC pundits were quick to hit out at Messi's behaviour as his team headed into extra time a man down.

Hart said: 'Oh wow! Wow! Yeah, I didn't enjoy that at all from Lionel Messi.

'You realise how on top Spain are if even Lionel Messi is reverting to that.'

Richards added: 'We don't want to see people getting sent off in a World Cup final for that.'

Rooney was similarly furious with Messi's behaviour as he said: 'It is desperation.

'Argentina play like that, we know that's what they do.

'But the one thing you want is good sportsmanship and that was sad to see Lionel Messi doing that.'

Sports.title: Distraught Lionel Messi bursts into tears as his World Cup career ends in heartbreak after brutal loss to Spain
Sports.content:
A heartbroken Lionel Messi burst into tears on the pitch after collecting his runners-up medal in what will almost certainly be his final ever World Cup appearance.

The Argentina captain - who spent most of his career playing in Barcelona - was ineffectual against Spain in the New Jersey showdown as his team failed to find the net in 120 minutes.

The tournament in America was almost certainly Messi's final international bow, and his emotional full-time reaction went some way to confirming that.

When the full-time whistle blew, he dropped to the ground and held his hands to his face, inconsolable by his teammates and opponents alike.

After gathering himself to collect his runners-up medal, the emotions of the moment became too much for the sport's greatest-of-all-time as he burst into tears just minutes before Spain lifted the trophy.

Messi's career will continue with Inter Miami but he is unlikely to play at the highest level again for his country, given he will be 43 when the next World Cup takes place.

Messi was appearing in his third World Cup final, four years after he lifted the trophy for his country in Qatar.

His first time in the biggest game of them all came in 2014 in Brazil, when he and his countrymen were beaten in extra-time by Germany.

It was the same result for the heartbroken Messi on Sunday, as Spain's Ferran Torres scored the only goal of the game deep into the additional 30-minute period.

More to follow.

Sports.title: Spain fans direct sarcastic chants of 'Infantino' at FIFA President after Nico Williams goal controversially disallowed - amid 'rigged' World Cup accusations
Sports.content:
Spain fans directed sarcastic chants at Gianni Infantino after Nico Williams saw a goal chalked off in extra-time for a 'soft' foul on Nicolas Otamendi.

With the score poised at 0-0 in the first-half of extra-time, the Spanish winger thought he'd won it when he slotted a side-footed effort under Emi Martinez.

But as Williams wheeled away to celebrate, Slovenian referee Slavko Vincic - taking charge of his first World Cup final - blew his whistle to signal a foul.

He deemed that Mikel Merino had trampled on the foot of Otamendi moments before Williams found the back of the net, causing the ex-Man City defender to collapse dramatically to the floor.

It was a decision which was reviewed but ultimately upheld by VAR, sparking fury in the stands at the 80,000-capacity MetLife Stadium.

The thousands of Spaniards who flocked to New Jersey were heard chanting 'Infantino', not for the first time during the match, amid accusations that the World Cup has been 'rigged' in the favour of Lionel Messi and Co.

Nico Williams was left bemused after seeing a goal in extra-time of the World Cup final disallowed

It came after Mike Merino was deemed to have trampled on the toes of Nicolas Otamendi

Infantino sat in the a suite at the MetLife Stadium with Donald Trump - before the pair presented the two teams with their medals after the match

Commentating on the game for the BBC, Alan Shearer said there was 'not enough' contact to warrant a foul.

'Was it just the way Mikel Merico went sliding in?', he questioned. 'That is not a foul for me.

'The only thing I can see is there is a slight touch of the toes on Nicolas Otamendi's toe, but not enough for me to give it as a free-kick.

'Otamendi makes a meal of it and that's what has won them the free-kick.'

The notion of a rigged World Cup is one which has plagued much of this tournament, with fans questioning whether referees have been biased towards Messi in what is almost certainly his final major tournament.

The South Americans struggled on their route to the World Cup final, only narrowly scraping past Cape Verde, Egypt and Switzerland in their earlier knockout games.

The manner of those victories - in which Egypt had a goal controversially disallowed and the Swiss saw striker Breel Embolo sent off - resulted in huge backlash surrounding the officiating of this summer's tournament.

Ex-Man City defender Manuel Akanji fumed after Switzerland were defeated by the Argentinians: 'Every little thing was called against us' and 'I've never experienced such a one-sided game.' Manager Murat Yakin called the refereeing 'incomprehensible'.

It came after Egypt winger Motafa Ziko argued: 'This tournament has been fixed', and his manager Hossam Hassan added: 'This match was rigged, and the whole world saw it.'

FIFA's chief refereeing officer Pierluigi Collina responded, stating that 'nobody can question the integrity' of the refereeing and 'unfounded allegations have no place in our sport'.

Ferran Torres won the final for Spain with a powerful finish in the 106th-minute

It sparked jubilant scenes as Spanish fans back in Madrid celebrated wildly together

Argentina's so-called luck, however, ultimately ran out in New Jersey on Sunday night as Spain rallied after the disallowed goal to find a winner.

It came through Ferran Torres in the 106th minute. After a ball was swung in from the right, Nico Williams nodded a header down from the far post, which the Barcelona striker latched on to and fired into the roof of the net to spark jubilant scenes.

The South Americans applied pressure of their own in search of a goal late on and Tottenham Hotspur defender Marcos Senesi almost levelled from close range.

But, in the end, it wasn't to be for Lionel Messi on what could his final appearance on football's biggest stage as Lamine Yamal and his Spanish team-mates held on for a historic victory.

Joe Hart said on the BBC: 'They were never rattled or under pressure. They haven't nibbled once. They played beautiful football the entire time.

'Yamal, at 19 years old, his confidence, the ways that he's doing this. Everyone will be trying to get on his back and hate on him, but he's got a Euros and World Cup. He kept so cool, kept his head, and had those standout moments.'

The match was, however, at times overshadowed by the antics of the Argentinians.

After taunting England's stars in Atlanta on Wednesday, Argentina's behaviour against Spain was dubbed 'embarrassing by pundits' after the final whistle in New Jersey.

Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez saw red in the 90+3-minute for a late challenge on Pau Cabarsi before chaotic scenes were sparked on the pitch when Spain's win was confirmed.

As the Spanish bench descended onto the pitch to celebrate, Argentinian substitute Leandro Paredes took issue with Barcelona midfielder Gavi.

The pair became embroiled in a row, causing Scaloni to intervene, before Paredes appeared to direct two punches at Gavi as he fell to the turf.

And, speaking on the BBC, ex-Man United striker Wayne Rooney was scathing in his criticism of Argentina's behaviour not only on Sunday, but throughout the tournament.

He said: 'It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this from Argentina before. It's just sad, very poor from them. If you lose a game of football, be graceful. It's a reaction to them being outplayed. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves it's well.'

Sports.title: Spain beat Argentina in World Cup final after Enzo Fernandez's moment of madness - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Ferran Torres was in the right place at the right time to mercifully settle a drab World Cup final in extra-time as Spain's dominance finally told against Argentina in New Jersey.

The reigning world champions, chasing history as they sought to become just the third team to ever win successive World Cups, failed to show up. Even with the genius of Lionel Messi in tow, Argentina were toothless on the biggest stage, failing to muster a single shot on goal until the 117th minute.

An uneventful first half slowly turned into a lulling Spain siege with Emi Martinez called into action to thwart Dani Olmo. It was the Aston Villa star keeping Argentina alive, making saves from Torres, Aymeric Laporte and numerous others as Spain increased the pressure.

Then, with extra-time looming, Enzo Fernandez was shown a second yellow card after the Chelsea midfielder went flying into Pau Cubarsi in a 50-50 near halfway to leave Argentina with a mountain to climb.

‌



Spain thought they finally had the goal their play merited in the early minutes of extra-time when Nico Williams smuggled the ball into the back of the net through a sea of bodies in the box before it was chalked off. But Argentina and Martinez's resistance was finally broken in the 106th minute when Torres plundered the winning goal.

Here are Mirror Football's talking points from the World Cup final...

World Cup final LIVE: Spain vs Argentina match and goal updates as Martinez suffers injury blow READ MORE :

Lisandro Martinez in floods of tears as Man Utd star suffers World Cup final agony READ MORE :

1. Argentina's fortune continues...until it doesn't

Unless you've been living under a rock for the last month, you'll probably be aware that Argentina have benefitted from some favourable officiating decisions. Egypt, eliminated in the most heartbreaking yet epic fashion by the defending world champions in the round of 16, even alleged there was a bias towards Lionel Scaloni's side from Fifa.

There were more than a few circumstances during the England-Argentina game where those in blue and white stripes were fortunate to avoid being reprimanded by the officials. And wherever you stand on such talk, Alexis Mac Allister escaping punishment for a late, reckless challenge on Dani Olmo early in the first half will do little to stifle such accusations.

‌



Maybe Argentina have just had the rub of the green on their way to tonight's final. But more than a few incidents during their enthralling run to the final, including Mac Allister's escape and the decision to rule out a Williams goal in extra-time for a soft foul on Nico Otamendi, have left an extremely sour taste.

2. A slow burn

View 5 Images Alexis Mac Allister was fortunate to escape punishment for a reckless challenge on Dani Olmo (Image: Daniela Porcelli)

Pre-match, the big question on the BBC's coverage of the final was over who would be the unfortunate soul to follow Jennifer Hudson and her epic performance of the American national anthem. But perhaps the real concern should have been over this match following the 10-goal thriller England and France served up in their bronze final less than 24 hours earlier.

Alright, the occasion isn't comparable and nerves and tension will have undoubtedly played a part in a drab first half, which saw the fewest shots (three, all for Spain) in any half of a World Cup final in history.

‌



For all the razzmatazz of the United States' big plans for its pre-match coverage, not to mention a half-time show, the action on the pitch didn't live up to the billing here. Even with an additional half an hour of play.

3. Fernandez's moment of madness

View 5 Images Enzo Fernandez was sent off in the final minutes of normal time

Not even Argentina and their good fortune could survive Fernandez and his stupid decision to go absolutely hurtling into Cubarsi in the final moments of extra-time. Already on a yellow card for dissent, there could only be one outcome.

Considering Argentina were pretty much under the pump for the whole game, Fernandez's cheap dismissal felt like the death knell for their chances of becoming just the third nation in history to win successive World Cups.

‌



Fernandez was distraught, but it was an absolute moment of madness from a player who rescued Argentina in their hour of need just days beforehand. If Fernandez saved Argentina's World Cup hopes with his stunner against England, then he absolutely killed them here.

4. Martinez's one-man stand v Spain

View 5 Images Emi Martinez kept Argentina alive in the World Cup final with save after save (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer/GES Sportfoto)

Spain dominated the game in regulation time when both sides had 11 men, so there was an air of inevitably about Spain's winning goal when it eventually did come in extra-time. But if one man on the pitch didn't deserve to be on the losing side, it was Martinez.

Heroic in Qatar four years ago as Argentina bested France on penalties, Martinez produced a performance on par with that in New Jersey, even if it was not enough to lift his country to yet more history.

‌



After springing to the turf to repel another Spain attempt, Martinez turned to whip up the crowd shortly after Fernandez's dismissal. But even Argentina's larger than life keeper was unable to deny Torres' powerful effort, Martinez finally beaten at the 12th attempt.

5. The Messi-Yamal final falls flat

View 5 Images Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal faced off in New Jersey (Image: Alex Livesey/Danehouse)

We've all seen the picture; that one of Messi crading a baby Yamal taken when the Argentine magician was a teenager with the world at his feet. This was the dream final that Fifa would have privately craved months ago: the one that pitted master vs apprentice, Messi against Yamal. Narrative wise, it was pitch-perfect.

Unfortunately, it transpired to be anything but. Both were ineffective and bystanders for large periods as Spain and Argentina sparred nervously for more than two hours.

‌



This has been a tournament where Messi, even at 39 years of age, has cemented has reputation as the world's undisputed best, orchestrating resurrections against Cape Verde, Egypt and England to propel Argentina to a second successive World Cup final. But their tournament ended with a whimper here; Argentina were practically non-existent as an attacking force, failing to muster a single attempt on goal in regulation time. This was a meek surrender.

In the case of Yamal, there were flashes of the genius that will almost certainly ensure he enjoys a long, fruitful reign as one of football's new icons. But like Messi, he too was on the periphery for much of this final. In truth, it's been that sort of tournament for Messi's Barcelona heir.

This World Cup will be remembered for many things. Unfortunately, the Messi-Yamal final will not be one of them.

Sports.title: Spain overwhelm dismal Argentina to win the World Cup for second time
Sports.content:
Finally justice was done in the MetLife Stadium.

The one team who came to play football won against the kings of anti-football.

Ferran Torres was Spain’s hero even if it needed extra time to see off Lionel Messi and Co as holders Argentina lost their grip on the World Cup trophy.

Messi’s dreams were left in tatters as this did not feel a remotely fitting way for one of football’s greatest players of all time to bow out if this proves to be his final act for his country.

‌



Argentina were dreadful, they did not manage a single shot on target and it felt as if they had no ambition to win the game. Enzo Fernandez was sent off in injury time at the end of 90 minutes and that just about summed up their ugly, spoiling and nasty approach.

And Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes greeted the final whistle by sparking a melee and swinging punches at celebrating Spain stars.

Wayne Rooney leaves BBC pundits speechless with brutal review of World Cup half-time show READ MORE :

Donald Trump brutally booed at World Cup final as Spain and Argentina fans unite READ MORE :

In contrast, Spain ushered in a new world order as the European champions now rule the world and they were utterly dominant in a final which did not really live up to its billing.

They thoroughly deserved their win and their stylish football helped us focus on the pitch and forget the silly showbiz that FIFA tried to impose on their showcase game.

‌



Spain had so many chances, so many near misses and Emiliano Martinez was Argentina’s hero with an incredible performance as he produced at least a dozen saves.

That is the one flaw in Spain’s make-up - they do not have a goal poacher who can finish off their wonderful, free-flowing approach play.

It needed a flick on from Nico Williams to set up Torres to finally seal the victory which sparked wild scenes of celebrations among the sea of red shirts in the crowd.

This was their day and a victory for football over spoilers but also helped the purists savour the game and quickly forget about lavish pre-match and half time shows.

‌



View 4 Images Lionel Messi during the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina

They had music, light shows and a bizarre half set which left most of the crowd cold amid the blazing sun in New Jersey.

The true football fans had come for the game and Argentina had just run out of dirty tricks, energy and legs after their exertions against England.

Mind you, Thomas Tuchel’s men must have been watching on from holiday and be thinking they would have given a better account of themselves than Argentina.

‌



They were woeful. Never looked like retaining their trophy - they wanted to become the first team since Brazil in 1962 to do that - and they looked a spent force.

View 4 Images Spain are champions of the world for the second time

Spain were bright, dominant and Rodri conducted them from midfield as they created chance after chance but were thwarted by Martinez.

Lamine Yamal did not really step up but had a good game and yet they just could not score. Lisandro Martinez went off injured for Argentina and they became the walking wounded after so many comebacks in this World Cup.

‌



Pedri, Torres and Mikel Merino all went close while Williams had an effort ruled out as you began to wonder whether they would score.

Even after Fernandez’s red card - for a second yellow after a foul on Pau Cubarsí - did not help Spain as Argentina dug in to try and hold on for penalties.

View 4 Images Enzo Fernandez was shown a red card in the closing stages of normal time

It felt like it was heading that way until Torres’ intervention. Then - and only then - did we see signs of life from Argentina.

‌



They pushed, Messi tried and they went close but Spain were superior and deserved their win.

This Argentina side looked to have reached the end of the road. Too many ageing players. Surely Messi will call it quits at 39 or he will certainly retire before the next World Cup.

Mentality and fight has carried them a long way in this tournament - and that is to be admired. If only England had as much.

But they were undone by a much better footballing side and Spain are now kings of the world again. And deservedly so.

‌

Sports.title: Lionel Messi slammed for desperate attempt to get Spain star sent off in World Cup final
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi slammed for desperate attempt to get Spain star sent off in World Cup final

Enzo Fernandez was sent off for Argentina during stoppage time in their World Cup final clash with Spain, but Lionel Messi also tried to get a Spain star red carded during the clash

View Image Lionel Messi tried to get Marc Cucurella sent off during the World Cup final (Image: BBC)

Lionel Messi was slammed by Wayne Rooney, Micah Richards and Joe Hart for trying to get Marc Cucurella sent off in sly fashion during the World Cup final. A moment of excitement sparked late into Argentina's clash with Spain at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, following a largely lacklustre 90 minutes, when Enzo Fernandez was given an early exit.

‌



The Chelsea star, who was already on a yellow for dissent earlier in the match, bundled through Pau Curbasi needlessly during stoppage time, sending him feet into the air with a dangling leg and leaving him in a heap on the floor. Referee Slavko Vincic didn't hesitate as he showed Fernandez a red card for the cynical foul, with immediate protests from the 25-year-old.

‌



However, it was during the furore that Messi attempted to immediately level the playing field by getting Cucurella sent off. Replays showed the Real Madrid full-back somewhat raising his hand to his face as he conversed with the Argentine captain.

‌



Donald Trump picks his World Cup winner and makes request to Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

Alan Shearer lets rip at 'stupid' Enzo Fernandez sent off in Spain vs Argentina World Cup final READ MORE :

While his mouth wasn't fully covered, a new rule from FIFA in a bid to rub out racism has been implemented for this summer's tournament, which prevents players from speaking to opponents with their mouths covered.

And while Cucurella may not have said anything sinister as he conversed with the 39-year-old, Messi was quick to flag to officials that Cucurella had covered his mouth.

The forward's pleas ultimately fell on deaf ears, however, as no action was taken against Cucurella.

‌



And as the two sides headed into extra time, the BBC panel of Rooney, Richards, Hart and Gabby Logan voiced their frustrations with the showing from one of the world's most respected players.

‌



Shocked by the move, Richards replied: "He's not got his whole hand over, he's got two fingers. It's harsh isn't it? You don't want to see people getting sent off in a World Cup final for that."

Hart then gave his two cents as he added: "Yeah, I didn't enjoy that at all.

"You realise how on top Spain are in this game if even Lionel Messi is reverting to that," before Logan replied: "Desperation from Messi there?"

Sports.title: Alan Shearer lets rip at 'stupid' Enzo Fernandez sent off in Spain vs Argentina World Cup final
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer lets rip at 'stupid' Enzo Fernandez sent off in Spain vs Argentina World Cup final

Alan Shearer did not hold back with his verdict of Enzo Fernandez's red card in the World Cup final

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez was shown a red card for a reckless challenge in the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina (Image: BBC Sport)

Alan Shearer ripped into Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernadez after he was sent off in the World Cup final clash with Spain. The Chelsea star had been shown a yellow card midway through the first half for dissent toward the match officials, before being shown a second yellow for a reckless foul on Pau Cubarsi just minutes before the final whistle.

‌



The game was edging toward extra-time when the 25-year-old went flying into a tackle on the halfway line, with Spain posing no real danger to his side. Cubarsi beat Fernandez to the ball, but the Argentinian midfielder made sure he left his mark on his opponent, upending the Spanish defender.

‌



Referee Slavko Vincic wasted no time in showing Fernandez a second yellow, but the Argentinian midfielder still remonstrated with the officials.

‌



Wayne Rooney leaves BBC pundits speechless with brutal review of World Cup half-time show READ MORE :

Lisandro Martinez in floods of tears as Man Utd star suffers World Cup final agony READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Lionel Messi and Fernandez were both seen arguing with the officials, appearing to call for Marc Cucurella to be shown a red card for covering his mouth with his hand after the original red card incident.

Nothing was given and the Argentinian midfielder was handed his marching orders.

‌



Speaking on co-commentary, Shearer said: "He might just have cost his team massively, because you know now that Argentina are going to try to take it to penalties. With him already being on a yellow card for something stupid - backchatting to the referee.

"And when you're on a yellow, you cannot, cannot make a challenge like that. That is stupid from him, it really is.

"I mean how daft is that from Enzo Fernandez? He's on a yellow card for dissent. Not for the tackel, for dissent. And he knows that, because that didn't happen long ago.

‌



"So for him to go into a challenge like that is crazy. He can protest as much as he wants, but it's the right decision. Gave the referee only one choice, and that was to issue another yellow - therefore the red."

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez was slammed by Alan Shearer after being shown a red card in the World Cup final clash against Spain. (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Wayne Rooney also gave a brutal verdict on the red card ahead of extra-time and said: "It's just a silly tackle. I think he's obviously a little bit late to it as we see here, and on a yellow card you can't just dangle your leg out and give the opposition an opportunity to get you a red card.

‌



"It's silly from Fernandez and it makes it a very different game now for Argentina to get through extra-time. Spain were on top as it was, but this makes it even more difficult."

Argentina did not register a single shot on goal inside the 90 minutes, even with 11 men on the pitch and managed just one touch inside the Spanish box.

Spain were the dominant side with 15 shots, ten of which were on target and 23 touches inside the opposition box, but weren't able to find a way past Emi Martinez as the game went into extra-time.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney leaves BBC pundits speechless with brutal review of World Cup half-time show
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney leaves BBC pundits speechless with brutal review of World Cup half-time show

Wayne Rooney made his feelings about the World Cup half-time show crystal clear

View Image Wayne Rooney was left furious (Image: BBC Sport)

Manchester United and England legend Wayne Rooney branded the World Cup final half-time show 'crap' in a brutally honest verdict. The opening 45 minutes of Argentina and Spain ended 0-0 with the European champions the better of the two sides at the break before a star-studded cast took to the pitch.

‌



The World Cup final has already come under major scrutiny with the pre-match show delaying kick-off by six minutes. While Donald Trump's appearance at the Met Life Stadium caused major delays for fans and members of the media getting into the ground due to heightened security measures.

‌



Spain were the more attacking of the two sides, with Argentina failing to register a single shot in the opening 45 minutes, while the European champions went close through Lamine Yamal and Mikel Oyarzabal.

‌

When the half-time whistle blew, players quickly left the field of play and it was a huge 27 minutes and 18 seconds until they returned, with the half-time show taking place.

As per the International Football Association Board rules, the half-time break should be no longer than 15 minutes, with the interval in breach of those rules.

‌



Justin Bieber, Madonna, Shakira, Gustavo Dudamel and BTS all performed in the half-time show, which was curated by Chris Martin from Coldplay. However, Rooney wasn't impressed.

Speaking on the BBC, Rooney said: "I'll be honest, mine (highlight) was when it finished. I like lot of those artists but I thought it was crap.

"I did, honestly. It just didn't get me going. I want the football to come back on. I like Burna Boy, I like Bieber, I like Shakira. That was flat."

‌

Micah Richards, who picked the performances of Shakira and Burna Boy as his highlights, called former international team-mate Rooney “miserable” for his frank assessment.

With the conversation following an advert promoting the BBC, host Gabby Logan added: “I’ll tell you what else you get on the BBC: honest reviews”.

‌



FIFA president Gianni Infantino announced plans for the show – which was curated by Coldplay frontman Chris Martin – in March last year.

Fans were left shocked to see Madonna arrive into the stadium on a buggy with Brazilian legends Ronaldo and Ronaldinho driving the cart.

One fan said: "Madonna, Ronaldo the Phenomenon, and Ronaldinho Gaúcho together - never thought I'd see this."

Sports.title: World Cup fans issue the same complaint about half-time show as Spain vs Argentina delayed
Sports.content:
World Cup fans issue the same complaint about half-time show as Spain vs Argentina delayed

The World Cup final between Spain and Argentina played host to an extended half-time break at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey as Coldplay, Justin Biber and Shakira took centre stage from Lionel Messi and co

View 3 Images The FIFA World Cup 2026 final half-time break lasted 27 minutes (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

World Cup final fans have fumed over the length of the half-time show at MetLife Stadium as Spain and Argentina were forced to take an extended break. The finalists were forced to wait a massive 27minutes and 18 seconds to return to the field.

‌



In an unprecedented move, FIFA's showpiece event saw a planned break that extended beyond the traditional 15 minutes. The show itself, comprising the likes of Madonna, Justin Bieber, Shakira and K-pop band BTS, was expected to be 11 minutes long with additional time required to set up and take down the performance infrastructure.

‌



World football's governing body declined to clarify how long the interval at this year's World Cup final would be on multiple occasions. But, after backlash over the possibility of a 30-minute break, the intention was for the break to last a total of 17 minutes.

‌



Safe to say, the break was too long for most fans, even in a match that was harder to watch than most.

"This is actually disgraceful I cant lie," said one fan on social media. Another said: "Horrendously long half time show that nobody cares to watch btw @FIFA do better"

Lisandro Martinez in floods of tears as Man Utd star suffers World Cup final agony READ MORE :

‌



"I much preferred football when it was a game of two halfs and half-time was barely long enough for the manager to swear at the players and throw teacups round the dressing room," added another.

"I hope with this really long half time, there won’t be another hydration break…" pleaded a further fan. "This half time show is over the top and too long. When is the second half starting?!" said another.

Coldplay's Chris Martin curated the performance, which also featured Nigerian singer Burna Boy, Philharmonic director Gustavo Dudamel, and PS22 Chorus featuring Coldplay. The likes of Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal were forced into an extended break in New Jersey.

‌



View 3 Images Ronaldinho, Madonna and Ronaldo started the half-time show (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

The BBC and ITV were initially not going to broadcast the show and planned to focus on the highlights and analysis from the opening 45 minutes. However, with the break extended, it was deemed possible to broadcast analysis and the on-pitch exploits at the break.

Gary Neville found something to like about the show. Speaking on ITV, he said: "I quite enjoyed it, let's hope the second half picks up and there's loads of energy in that."

‌



On BBC, Wayne Rooney's verdict was less kind. "I'll be honest, mine (highlight) was when it finished," he said.

View 3 Images Justin Bieber performs (Image: Getty Images)

"I like lot of those artists but I thought it was crap. I did, honestly. It just didn't get me going. I want the football to come back on. I like Burna Boy, I like Bieber, I like Shakira. That was flat."

Last summer, FIFA also saw an extended break for the Club World Cup final. They flaunted the rules regarding the length of time between halves for the clash between Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain where the interval stretched to 25 minutes.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez in floods of tears as Man Utd star suffers World Cup final agony
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez in floods of tears as Man Utd star suffers World Cup final agony

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez suffered a cruel injury blow during the first half of the World Cup final

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez was in tears after being forced off with an injury in the World Cup final against Spain (Image: (Photo by Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images))

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez was spotted in floods of tears after being forced off the pitch during the World Cup final against Spain. The 28-year-old started the final in the heart of defence alongside Tottenham Hotspur defender Cristian Romero, but had to be replaced just before the half-time interval with an injury.

‌



It was a tight, nervy first half display from both teams, though Spain looked the most likely to score with Argentina failing to register a single shot inside the opening 45 minutes. Marc Cucurella had just curled an effort just wide of Emi Martinez's goal in the 43rd minute, when Martinez hit the floor.

‌



The United defender had been booked for a late foul on Mikel Oyarzabal just moments earlier, for stopping a Spanish counter attack in its tracks. However, 'The Butcher' was unable to continue and was replaced by former Manchester City defender Nicolas Otamendi in the 44th minute.

‌



Donald Trump brutally booed at World Cup final as Spain and Argentina fans unite READ MORE :

Gary Lineker makes instant England prediction after France and responds to Bukayo Saka READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Martinez left the pitch in tears after being unable to carry on. The former United defender was consoled by Martinez before making his way off the pitch.

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez is consoled by Emi Martinez before he is replaced in the World Cup final vs Spain (Image: (Photo by Hector Vivas - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

‌



The United defender has been a mainstay in the Argentina defence en route to the final, but was visibly distraught after making his way off. He was seen crying, with his head in his hands on the bench.

Argentina were second best throughout the first half, with Spain boasting 65 per cent possession, registering three shots, two of which came on target.

The European champions got off to a fast start when Lamine Yamal burst into the box just five minutes into the game. The Barcelona winger tried to cross into the box, but the ball fell to Dani Olmo on the edge of the area.

‌



The Barca playmaker found Yamal in acres of space inside the 18-yard box, driving to the byline and trying to pick out the bottom corner.

However, a combination of both Lisandro Martinez and Emi Martinez kept the young Spanish star at bay.

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez's World Cup final participation was cut short (Image: BBC Sport)

Article continues below

Argentina were content to sit behind the ball with Lionel Messi as their sole man in attack. Spain kept probing and Oyarzabal called Martinez into action again in the 39th minute.

Fabian Ruiz poked the ball through to the Spanish striker, who rifled a first time left-footed effort down low into the corner, but Martinez was equal to it, keeping the score locked at 0-0 at the half-time interval.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
