World.title: Panama Bill Would Require Influencers to Disclose Paid Posts
World.content:
Panama’s National Assembly is considering a bill that would require social media influencers and content creators to clearly identify when their posts are paid advertising rather than independent recommendations. Deputy Walkiria Chandler D’Orcy, a member of the Vamos coalition, presented the proposal to the Assembly plenary on July 13, 2026. The measure aims to stop what she described as hidden advertising that takes advantage of the trust followers place in creators.

“What the user does not know is that many times behind that recommendation there is advertising, there is a contract, there is a payment, there is some product that has been given to that influencer or a commission for each sale… it seems to be an opinion, it is really advertising that was not identified as such,” Chandler said during the presentation.

She linked the bill to Panama’s existing consumer protection rules under Law 45 of 2007. That law already requires advertising to be presented clearly so consumers are not misled. Chandler argued that sponsored content on digital platforms often fails this standard and that stronger rules are needed, especially for younger audiences.

The proposal would require creators to make commercial content identifiable. Chandler stressed that the rules would cover promotions involving cash, contracts, free products, or commissions. She said the measure would not create new state registries or add budget costs. Chandler highlighted stronger protections for minors. She noted that many social media users are young and may have greater difficulty distinguishing genuine opinions from paid promotions.

The bill remains at an early stage. As of now, it has been presented to the full Assembly but has not advanced through committee debate or further votes. Details on specific labeling requirements, penalty amounts, the exact number of articles, or an implementation timeline have not been confirmed in official records or public statements beyond the presentation.

Influencer marketing has grown across Latin America as brands use creators to reach audiences on platforms such as Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. Panama’s consumer authority has previously reminded businesses that online advertising must still comply with Law 45 rules on truthful claims and clear presentation. Chandler’s proposal seeks to apply those principles more directly to the influencer model.

If the Assembly moves the bill forward, it would join other regional efforts to address transparency in digital advertising. For now, the proposal stands as an attempt to give Panamanian consumers clearer signals about when content is commercial.

World.title: Costa Rica Bridge to Manuel Antonio Faces “Imminent Failure” Warning
World.content:
A bridge on the main car route toward one of Costa Rica’s most-visited places has been flagged as at risk of collapse, according to a special inspection carried out by the Laboratorio Nacional de Materiales y Modelos Estructurales (Lanamme) at the University of Costa Rica.

The structure spans the Boca Vieja estuary at kilometer 2.17 of Route 235, the secondary road that links central Quepos with the community of La Managua and the corridor leading to Manuel Antonio, home to the national park of the same name and a cornerstone of the central Pacific tourism economy.

Lanamme engineers assigned the bridge a rating of “imminent failure,” the most severe classification in the laboratory’s system, after finding severe corrosion running the full length of the superstructure’s main girders. The deterioration is most acute along roughly 12 meters (39 feet) at each end of the span, a pattern the report warns could lead to a collapse of the superstructure in the short term.

The bridge is not an aging relic. It opened in December 2016, built by the Ministerio de Obras Públicas y Transportes (MOPT) and the Consejo Nacional de Vialidad (Conavi) at a cost the ministry put at ₡1.56 billion (roughly US$3 million), and was promoted at the time as a modern two-lane concrete replacement that would improve access to a region the government itself described as having high tourism potential. Less than a decade later, the same authorities are being told the structure may not be safe to carry the traffic it was designed for.

Lanamme recommended an immediate detailed inspection and a load-capacity analysis to establish the maximum weight the bridge can safely bear, followed by inclusion of the structure in a short-term program of major rehabilitation or reconstruction. The report frames the corrosion as a known and worsening problem rather than a sudden discovery, pointing to a documented decline in the bridge’s condition over time.

As of yet, neither the MOPT nor Conavi had announced traffic restrictions, load limits, or emergency repairs in response to the warning. That leaves drivers, tour operators, and shuttle services heading to and from Manuel Antonio using a bridge that engineers have rated one step from failure, with no posted guidance on whether it should still carry heavy vehicles.

For an area whose economy depends heavily on visitor access, an unplanned closure of the Boca Vieja crossing — whether ordered by authorities or forced by further deterioration — would sever a primary route into the tourism zone with no obvious substitute.

World.title: Costa Rica ‘sold itself’ to Washington for visa power, says Óscar Arias
World.content:
Former President and Nobel Peace laureate Óscar Arias has accused Costa Rica of surrendering its foreign-policy independence to the United States, telling a San José television program that it “sold itself” for the leverage Washington holds over which members of the political class keep an American visa.

The remarks aired on the program La Reacción in an interview conducted by journalist Danilo Chaves. Pressed by the interviewer on whether Costa Rica had sold itself for very little, Arias framed the wave of visa revocations in recent years as a bargaining chip that has eroded national autonomy.

He described the arrangement as trading the country’s standing for the “toy” of a president being able to tell Washington to strip the visa of one figure after another — a deputy, a magistrate, a former president, the president of the Legislative Assembly — adding sardonically that the only name still missing from the list was the bishop of San José.

The tone marked a shift for Arias. In April 2025, when the U.S. State Department revoked his own visa, he had said he did not believe the Costa Rican government bore any responsibility for Washington’s decisions, calling it a matter for the United States alone. In the interview he went further, suggesting the revocations have served domestic political ends and arguing that the United States dictates terms to any country that allows it to.

Arias also contended that aligning with one global power at the expense of another has been a strategic error, pointing to the cooling of relations with China. He held up El Salvador’s president, Nayib Bukele, as a leader who has managed to maintain ties with both Washington and Beijing, citing the Chinese-financed national stadium in San Salvador as evidence that a country can pursue beneficial relationships without geopolitical exclusivity. Costa Rican foreign policy, he said, should prioritize balance and autonomy rather than leaving itself exposed to measures such as visa revocations.

The revocations Arias referenced have accumulated over more than a year and have touched a widening circle of public figures. Reporting listed Arias himself; his brother, former Legislative Assembly president Rodrigo Arias Sánchez; former independent deputy Johana Obando Bonilla; magistrate Fernando Cruz Castro; and directors of the newspaper La Nación among those affected.

Arias’s own revocation came weeks after he compared U.S. President Donald Trump to a Roman emperor on social media; U.S. Embassy staff, he said at the time, attributed the move to his close ties with the Chinese government. Costa Rica established diplomatic relations with China in 2007, during Arias’s second term.

The close alignment with Washington took shape under former President Rodrigo Chaves Robles, whose administration excluded Chinese firms from the country’s 5G rollout following U.S. pressure, and it has continued under current President Laura Fernández Delgado. Trump recently sent Fernández a gift, a gesture read in San José as a reaffirmation of the bilateral relationship. Successive Costa Rican governments, the U.S. Embassy and the State Department have all declined to discuss individual cases or give reasons for specific revocations.

Whether the current administration will respond directly to Arias’s characterization remains to be seen. For now, his intervention reopens a debate that has run beneath Costa Rican politics since the first revocations landed: how much of its traditional diplomatic independence a small country can retain when access to the United States has become a lever in its own internal disputes

World.title: Belize basks in sunshine while a depression may form up north
World.content:
Belize basks in sunshine while a depression may form up north

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Belize gets the Sunday it hoped for. Mostly sunny skies, warm temperatures, and calm seas set the stage for World Cup final day, while forecasters keep a distant eye on a system taking shape far to the north in the Gulf of Mexico.

According to the National Meteorological Service, a light, warm, and mostly dry easterly airflow prevails. Skies will be mostly sunny today, turning clear to partly cloudy tonight, with any showers staying isolated, ideal conditions for wherever you plan to watch Spain and Argentina contest the final at 1:00 p.m.

The tropical outlook carries a new note, though not one for Belizean alarm. A broad surface low located over the northeastern Gulf of Mexico has a high chance of becoming a tropical depression later today or tomorrow. That system sits far to Belize’s north, well away from our shores, and the Met Service confirms that elsewhere in the region, including our area, tropical cyclone formation is not expected over the next 48 hours. It is a development worth following, nothing more for now.

Temperatures along the coast will reach a high of 89 degrees Fahrenheit (32 Celsius) and a low of 82 (28 Celsius). Inland areas will be hot, climbing to 94 degrees Fahrenheit (34 Celsius) and dropping to 74 (23 Celsius). In the hills, expect a high of 82 degrees Fahrenheit (28 Celsius) and a low of 68 (20 Celsius).

At sea, conditions stay gentle, with easterly winds of 5 to 15 knots, a light chop, and waves of 2 to 4 feet, another fine day on the water.

Looking ahead to Monday and Monday night, the fair and warm pattern continues, with shower activity, if any, remaining isolated.

Today’s low tides are at 7:54 AM and 8:10 PM, with a high tide at 1:42 PM and another high at 2:11 AM tomorrow. The sun rose at 5:27 AM and will set at 6:30 PM. The forecast was issued by forecaster Catherine Cumberbatch.

World.title: Spain vs Argentina today: the final of dreams, who wins it?
World.content:
Spain vs Argentina today: the final of dreams, who wins it?

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): This is the one. Spain and Argentina, the number two and number one ranked teams on the planet, meet today at 1:00 p.m. Belize time at MetLife Stadium to decide the World Cup, and across the Jewel, a nation painted in blue and white holds its breath.

The stakes could not be written any larger. Argentina, the defending champions, stand ninety minutes from back-to-back World Cup titles, a feat achieved only twice in history.

And at the centre of it all is Lionel Messi, playing what is expected to be the final World Cup match of the greatest career football has known. The golden boot picture shifted on Saturday, when Kylian Mbappé struck twice in France’s wild 6-4 third-place defeat to England, taking his tournament tally to ten, two clear of Messi’s eight, and claiming the all-time World Cup scoring record with 22. To snatch the boot back today, Messi needs nothing less than a hat trick, or two goals and an assist. A second straight crown, though, requires only a win, and back-to-back titles would complete a legacy no scoring chart can measure.

But standing in the way is the most formidable obstacle this tournament could offer. Spain, the European champions, have conceded exactly one goal in seven matches, a defensive record that borders on unreal. They dismantled France 2-0 in the semi-final with a team goal, the Porro and Olmo one-two, already being hailed among the tournament’s finest, and they arrive as the bookmakers’ favourite, with the numbers giving La Roja roughly a 41 percent chance to Argentina’s 27, and a meaningful chance this goes the distance to extra time.

Argentina’s answer is written in scar tissue. The champions have stared down elimination repeatedly, storming back from 2-0 down against Egypt with three late goals, outlasting Switzerland in extra time, and then, in Wednesday’s semi-final, beating England 2-1 to end a forty-year wait against their fiercest rival. This team does not know when it is beaten, and in Messi it carries the one player on Earth capable of deciding any match alone.

So the question is the oldest one in sport: does the immovable object or the unstoppable story win? Spain’s control, discipline, and near-perfect machine, or Argentina’s champions’ heart and the destiny of the greatest of all time?

A projected 1.8 billion people worldwide will watch it decided, and few places will live it more intensely than Belize, where the Albiceleste’s army has waited all tournament for this day. At 1:00 p.m., the country stops.

So make your call, Belize, and make it loud: Spain or Argentina, who lifts the World Cup today? Drop your prediction and your final score in the comments.

World.title: Ten goals of madness: England beat France 6-4 for third place
World.content:
Ten goals of madness: England beat France 6-4 for third place

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): They call the third-place match the game nobody wants to play. Somebody forgot to tell England and France, who produced one of the most extraordinary matches in World Cup history on Saturday, a ten-goal spectacle that England won 6-4 to claim the bronze, while Kylian Mbappé rewrote the record books even in defeat.

The numbers alone belong in a museum. As the Associated Press reported, it was the highest-scoring World Cup game since Hungary beat El Salvador 10-1 back in 1982, and the ten goals were the most ever scored in a third-place match.

England did the early demolition. Declan Rice opened in just the third minute, Ezri Konsa doubled the lead, and Bukayo Saka struck twice, in the 37th minute and in first-half stoppage time, to send the Three Lions in at half-time an astonishing 4-0 up. With France facing humiliation in coach Didier Deschamps’ final game in charge, the rout looked on.

Then came the fightback. France roared out after the break, with Mbappé scoring twice either side of a Bradley Barcola goal to claw it back to 4-3 and set up a frantic finish. Les Bleus pushed for the equaliser, but Saka completed his hat trick from the penalty spot in the 87th minute, and though Ousmane Dembélé pulled another back in the dying moments, England struck once more at the death to seal a 6-4 win and their best World Cup finish since lifting the trophy in 1966. Notably, England did it all without captain Harry Kane, who did not feature, ending his tournament on six goals.

Mbappé’s consolation was historic. His brace took his tournament tally to ten goals and, as Euronews reported, carried him past Lionel Messi on the all-time World Cup scoring list with 22 career goals to Messi’s 21. It also stretched his golden boot lead to two, ten goals to Messi’s eight, meaning, per ESPN’s breakdown of FIFA’s tiebreakers, Messi needs a hat trick, or two goals and an assist, in today’s final against Spain to snatch the award back.

And that is the beauty of it: even the consolation game ended up pouring fuel on today’s main event. The bronze is England’s. The records are Mbappé’s. The stage, at 1:00 p.m. Belize time, belongs to Messi, Argentina, and Spain.

Did you catch the ten-goal madness, Belize? And can Messi answer Mbappé today? Comment below.

World.title: US and Iran trade strikes again as Washington avenges American deaths
World.content:
Iran’s joint military command said in a statement carried by state media that U.S. “covetousness, bullying, totalitarianism or brutality” would meet a “devastating response.”

Iranian strikes hit a Kuwaiti power and water desalination plant for the second time in two days, Kuwait’s electricity ministry said, sparking a fire in a country that relies on desalination for about 90 percent of its drinking water.

Bahrain reported intercepting attacks, and Jordan said it shot down three of four Iranian missiles aimed toward its territory.

Israel warned that projectiles fired toward the port city of Aqaba could spill over into its territory for the first time in weeks.

U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright insisted Sunday that oil is still moving through the Hormuz channel despite the fighting, telling ABC’s “This Week” program that flows from the Gulf region stand at just under 14 million barrels a day, or two-thirds of pre-conflict traffic. “Almost all the public data I’ve seen is incorrect,” he said.

Iran’s atomic energy agency said U.S. strikes hit the unfinished Darkhovin nuclear power plant in Khuzestan province. The International Atomic Energy Agency said it was investigating and that the site, still in early construction, holds no nuclear material and poses no radiological risk. Iranian authorities said 50 people have been killed and 517 wounded in the latest American strikes.

Iran’s supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, said Saturday that U.S. President Donald Trump’s signature on the interim deal was “utterly worthless and devoid of credibility.”

Asked about Tehran abandoning the deal, Trump told NewsNation: “I couldn’t care less.”

World.title: Merz floats government reshuffle after top conservative’s resignation
World.content:
Asked about Thorsten Frei, his chief of staff, whom ZDF has floated as a possible successor to Spahn, Merz declined to confirm any names. Promoting Frei would leave Merz with another senior vacancy to fill.

In the interview, Merz also declined to defend Spahn personally, saying he had not expected outrage “on this scale.” “It probably also had something to do with his person, and also with the communication,” the chancellor said.

Merz said Spahn told him about the child around 10 days ago and asked him to keep it quiet, which he did. Spahn informed the party “very, very late,” Merz said, and the damage to its credibility became “abundantly clear” on Saturday. “And that’s why we then acted.”

German media reported Saturday that Merz had asked Spahn to step down.

Asked whether he felt betrayed, Merz said only that he did not want to assess it publicly. He called the matter closed and thanked Spahn for his work on the governing coalition’s recent reforms.

The CDU party leadership is expected to discuss the succession in the coming days, according to ZDF.

World.title: Russia hits Ukraine with one of the largest ballistic barrages of the war
World.content:
Acting Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called it the largest ballistic attack of the war. Ukraine’s air force put it lower, saying it was one of the largest and the fourth strike of comparable size on Kyiv in the past five weeks. It said it shot down 18 of the 41 missiles and downed nearly all of those on a ballistic trajectory.

The strikes damaged residential buildings, a supermarket and a dormitory in the capital, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. At least one person in Kyiv was killed in the attack and 15 wounded, Ukrainian officials said.

Russia’s defense ministry said it had hit what it called defense industry facilities and logistics centers in Kyiv.

The interceptor shortage has worsened since the war with Iran, which drained U.S. and allied Patriot stocks. Zelenskyy has said Ukraine needs 300 Patriots for the coming winter. U.S. President Donald Trump said this month he would let Ukraine produce the missiles under license, but the arrangement has not been finalized.

Nine European countries agreed on July 13 to back a Ukrainian effort to build a homegrown anti-ballistic system, and France is licensing Ukraine to produce its Aster interceptors.

Ukrainian officials also pressed the EU to break its deadlock over a new sanctions package.

World.title: Tate brothers arrested in US as Britain unveils new rape and trafficking charges
World.content:
Britain’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said on Sunday that it will prosecute Andrew Tate, 39, on new counts of rape along with charges of trafficking for sexual exploitation, assault and offenses relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography. Tristan Tate, 38, faces new counts of rape, sexual assault and trafficking for sexual exploitation.

The 38 new charges come on top of 21 the brothers already face in Britain, and bring the total number of alleged victims to seven. They relate to alleged offenses between July 2010 and August 2017, the CPS said.

“They have been arrested and await extradition proceedings to the U.K.,” said Malcolm McHaffie, head of the Special Crime Division at the CPS.

The U.S. Justice Department said the arrests were carried out under standard extradition procedures. “Today, U.S. Marshals in the Southern District of Florida arrested Andrew and Tristan Tate pursuant to extradition proceedings,” a department spokesperson said Saturday. “These arrests were made in accordance with the treaties and law enforcement agreements governing Justice Department extraditions.”

The arrest warrant remains sealed, and the Tates are expected to make an initial court appearance in Florida early next week, according to a law enforcement official.

The pair moved to Romania in 2016, were arrested there in 2022 in a separate sexual exploitation investigation, and traveled to the U.S. after a Romanian travel ban was lifted last year.

The Tates, former kickboxers with dual U.S. and British citizenship, built their fame promoting a lavish lifestyle and views on masculinity and wealth. Andrew Tate has previously described himself as a misogynist. Both brothers deny all the allegations against them.

Josh Gerstein contributed reporting.

World.title: Spain win World Cup for second time after thrilling final against Argentina
World.content:
Ferran Torres sealed Spain's second World Cup title on Sunday with the only goal of the final, smashing home from close range after reacting to a loose ball in the penalty area in extra time. The strike finally broke the deadlock after more than 100 minutes of play.

 

Luis de la Fuente's side made the brighter start, dominating possession and looking to exploit spaces between the lines against a well-organised Argentina defence.

The first clear chance came after five minutes when Lamine Yamal combined with Dani Olmo before forcing a close-range save from goalkeeper Emiliano "Dibu" Martínez. Minutes later, Yamal threatened again after a perfectly weighted pass from Rodri, but Argentina's defenders cleared the danger.

Lionel Scaloni's Argentina looked to hit on the counter through Lionel Messi and Julián Álvarez but were repeatedly denied by Spain goalkeeper Unai Simón, who was quick off his line to intercept several dangerous attacks.

Spain continued to dictate the tempo through Rodri in midfield, while Álex Baena, Mikel Oyarzabal and Marc Cucurella all found space down the left flank.

Marc Cucurella pushed forward throughout the match as Spain searched for the opening goal. Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.

The game became increasingly physical as the first half wore on, with players also having to contend with a dry, uneven pitch and high temperatures.

Referee Slavko Vinčić waved play on after a robust challenge by Nicolás Tagliafico on Lamine Yamal but later booked Lisandro Martínez for bringing down Oyarzabal as Spain launched a counterattack. Martínez was forced off injured shortly before half-time and replaced by Nicolás Otamendi.

Spain finished the first half strongly, with Oyarzabal forcing another save from Martínez before Cucurella sent a powerful effort narrowly wide of the post.

Argentina rarely threatened going forward beyond a handful of attacks down the right and isolated moments involving Messi and Álvarez, leaving the score goalless at the break in a finely balanced final.

Second half remains goalless as tensions rise

The second half followed a similar pattern to the first, with Spain dominating possession while Argentina relied on an aggressive press and a physical approach.

Lionel Scaloni made an immediate change after the restart, introducing Leandro Paredes, whose arrival added further intensity to the contest. The midfielder was quickly booked after catching Rodri off the ball and was involved in several heated exchanges as the match became increasingly fragmented by fouls and stoppages.

Spain gradually tightened their grip on the game and created a series of chances to break the deadlock. Álex Baena tried his luck from distance, Lamine Yamal's free kick was blocked by the wall and Dani Olmo forced Emiliano Martínez into a fine save with a low effort that bounced awkwardly in front of the goalkeeper.

Spain also threatened from set pieces, winning a succession of corners as Marc Cucurella, Pedro Porro and Pau Cubarsí regularly pushed forward.

Luis de la Fuente freshened up his side by introducing Pedri and Ferran Torres for Fabián Ruiz and Mikel Oyarzabal, before later sending on Nico Williams and Mikel Merino in place of Olmo and Baena.

Scaloni responded with Nahuel Molina, Facundo Medina and Giuliano Simeone in an attempt to contain Spain's pressure while looking to exploit counterattacks through Lionel Messi and Julián Álvarez. However, Spain's defence, marshalled by Cubarsí, Aymeric Laporte and goalkeeper Unai Simón, allowed Argentina few clear opportunities.

Spain increased the pressure in the closing stages of normal time. Ferran Torres headed straight at Martínez before Pedri and Cubarsí again tested the Argentina goalkeeper, while Laporte went close with a header from a corner.

The momentum shifted dramatically in stoppage time when Enzo Fernández was sent off after receiving a second yellow card for a reckless challenge on Cubarsí, reducing Argentina to 10 men. Spain pushed relentlessly for a late winner, but Martínez and a deep-lying Argentina defence held firm as tempers flared in the closing moments.

Torres strikes late to seal Spain's second World Cup title

Extra time also began without a breakthrough, with both teams continuing to battle for control as chances remained scarce. But early in the second period of extra time, Spain finally found the goal it had been searching for.

Then, in the 106th minute, Lamine Yamal laid the ball off to Pedro Porro on the right edge of the penalty area, and the defender delivered a cross towards the far post. Under pressure from Nahuel Molina, Nico Williams opted not to attempt a header from a tight angle, instead nodding the ball back into the centre of the box. Ferran Torres arrived to meet it with a powerful left-footed volley that flew into the roof of the net.

Argentina came alive in the closing stages, but their late push was not enough to prevent Spain from being crowned world champions.

As the final whistle blew, Spain were crowned world champions for the second time, completing an unbeaten run through the tournament and ending Argentina's reign.

World.title: Heading for the North Pole on Tara Polar Station's first expedition
World.content:
TheTara Polar Station_,_ a scientific research station designed to drift with the sea ice, left the port of Lorient on Sunday afternoon on its first expedition to the North Pole. Several hundred people gathered along the quays to watch the departure, in the presence of the Minister for the Sea, Catherine Chabaud.

 

The crew’s objective on board the floating saucer is to gain a better understanding of the biodiversity of the Arctic Ocean and the effects of global warming in this region, which is heating up three to four times faster than the rest of the planet and where the sea ice is retreating at a rapid pace.

Twelve countries, including Germany, Canada, the United States, Spain, Switzerland and Japan, are taking part in the mission.

Shaped like an igloo set on an immense buoy, the Tara Polar Stationhas been designed to withstand the pressure of the sea ice and temperatures as low as −52 °C.

From mid-August, it will sail along the Russian coast, escorted by an icebreaker. Once it is caught in the pack ice at the beginning of September, it will allow itself to be carried by the drifting ice for 350 to 500 days, moving at an average speed of around ten kilometres a day towards the Fram Strait, between Greenland and Svalbard, where it is expected to arrive at the end of 2027.

A mission at the heart of the ice

Twelve people will live on board during the winter, including six scientists, and eighteen during the summer. The crew members, selected after a series of medical and psychological tests, have also taken part in a team-building seminar to prepare for this long mission in extreme conditions.

The overwintering crew will have to contend with five months of polar night, average temperatures of −25 °C and the presence of polar bears.

To ensure their safety during trips out onto the ice, all crew members have been trained in the use of firearms. A Lapponian herder dog will also accompany the mission to detect any approaching animals.

Gaining a better understanding of a rapidly changing Arctic

Thanks to a well built at the heart of the station and state-of-the-art scientific instruments, researchers will take more than 10,000 samples from the water column, down to a depth of 2,000 metres, as well as from the atmosphere and cavities within the sea ice.

Scientists hope in this way to collect data on Arctic biodiversity, still largely unknown, before the region is profoundly transformed.

Several programmes will also help to improve climate models, in particular by studying the role of bacteria in the reflectivity of clouds.

The cost of this first mission is estimated at 6 million euros. It marks the launch of a programme of ten expeditions scheduled between 2026 and 2045, with one mission every two years.

World.title: Trump and Sánchez meet at World Cup final after nearly two years of diplomatic tensions
World.content:
After nearly two years of public tensions and failed attempts to improve relations, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and US President Donald Trump came face to face on Sunday at the 2026 FIFA World Cup final in New Jersey.

 

The two leaders were seated in the VIP section at MetLife Stadium, where Spain faced Argentina. Spain's King Felipe VI, Queen Letizia and Princesses Leonor and Sofía also attended the match.

The brief encounter comes after months of friction between Washington and Madrid over defence spending. Relations have eased in recent weeks, however, after Trump said Spain had "fully redeemed itself" by agreeing to a substantial increase in its NATO defence commitments at last month's summit in Ankara.

The shift marked a sharp contrast with Trump's remarks during the summit, when he described Spain as a "lost cause" and threatened trade retaliation. On his return to Washington, however, he adopted a more conciliatory tone.

Sánchez has maintained that Spain has "more than fulfilled its obligations" by significantly increasing defence spending.

Hours before the meeting, Sánchez used an interview with Spanish public broadcaster RTVE to congratulate Trump on the 250th anniversary of the United States, which is being celebrated this week.

Asked whether Trump might present the World Cup trophy to the winners, the Spanish prime minister avoided speculation, saying: "What matters to me is not who presents it, but who receives it."

While the Spanish delegation attended in full, Argentina's President Javier Milei was absent from the VIP section after saying earlier this week he would not travel to the final because of a superstition.

Speaking to Fox News before the match, Trump described Milei as a "friend" and, when asked about the final, said: "It's hard to bet against Messi."

The main source of tension between the two governments remains defence spending. Spain has yet to commit to NATO's target of spending 5% of GDP on defence, a goal championed by Washington that Sánchez has described as "unreasonable and counterproductive".

The relationship has also been strained by differences over the war in Gaza. Spain has described Israel's military campaign as a genocide, a characterisation rejected by the United States.

Tensions deepened further after the conflict between the United States and Iran. Madrid invoked its bilateral defence agreement with Washington to prohibit the use of the US military bases at Rota and Morón for operations linked to the conflict.

World.title: German Chancellor Merz hints at possible cabinet reshuffle after top CDU figure resigns
World.content:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has signalled he is open to reshuffling his government as he seeks to fill the vacancy left by CDU parliamentary leader Jens Spahn, who was asked to step down and eventually resigned on Saturday.

 

Speaking in ZDF's summer interview, Merz stressed he was speaking "hypothetically", but said he wants a decision on Spahn's successor as leader of the CDU/CSU parliamentary group in Germany's Bundestag by the end of July.

Chancellery Minister Thorsten Frei is widely seen as the frontrunner to replace Spahn, although Merz declined to confirm whether Frei or any other candidate was under consideration.

If Frei were to become parliamentary leader, Merz would also need to appoint a new head of the Chancellery, one of the chancellor's closest aides responsible for coordinating government policy.

Friedrich Merz with Chancellery Minister Thorsten Frei on 15 July 2026 Ebrahim Noroozi/Copyright 2026 The AP. All rights reserved

The pressure to resolve the issue quickly is also driven by a series of key state elections in September in Saxony-Anhalt, Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. The CDU is facing difficult contests in all three states.

In Saxony-Anhalt, the far-right AfD is hoping to secure its first state premiership, with lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund. The party's regional branch in the state has been classified by Germany's domestic intelligence agency as a confirmed far-right extremist organisation.

Spahn has come under particular scrutiny after he and his husband became fathers through surrogacy in the United States, a process that can cost hundreds of thousands of euros. The issue has also reignited debate over Germany's restrictive surrogacy laws.

Critics on the political left and within the Green party have accused Spahn of hypocrisy as he has repeatedly opposed legalising surrogacy in Germany and has not backed broader reforms to family policy.

Jens Spahn as health minister in 2021 Tobias Schwarz/AP

Merz said he had not expected the backlash against Spahn to be "to this extent". Speaking to ZDF, the chancellor said there had been "quite a lot of outrage" directed at the CDU politician and suggested the criticism was "probably also related to him as a person and the way it was communicated".

Asked whether the controversy risked damaging the CDU/CSU ahead of key regional elections, Merz said: "Over the course of yesterday it became overwhelmingly clear to me, and that is why we acted."

The affair comes as Merz is facing mounting political pressure of his own. Just two months before a series of important regional elections, only 13% of Germans say they are satisfied with his performance as chancellor, while around five in six are dissatisfied, according to the latest ARD-DeutschlandTrend poll.

The survey also found that no previous German chancellor had recorded lower approval ratings at this stage of their time in office than Merz.

World.title: Spain win World Cup for second time after beating Argentina 1-0
World.content:
After a 16 year wait, Spain have claimed a second men's World Cup. Ferran Torres scored the winner in a deserved 1-0 victory over Argentina, which means Spain are now men’s and women’s world champions.

Patience proved the critical virtue for Spain. They had to wait for a kickoff delayed by — among other things — a Tom Cruise speech. They had to wait twice as long as usual at half time. And they had to wait for 106 minutes of play and their 20th shot before Ferran Torres lashed home the goal that would win them a second men's World Cup.

"I’m very moved. Looking back and thinking about them, we’ve won everything, absolutely everything, with this generation of players," said Spain coach Luis de la Fuente. "The match should have been decided much earlier ... but this is a World Cup final and you have to dig deep even against ten men, and we’re prepared for anything."

Spain's captain and player of the tournament, Rodri, lifted the trophy. But not before Donald Trump made his presence known. The US president was booed when he entered the pitch with FIFA president, Gianni Infantino and appeared keen to stay for the trophy lift, just as he had in the Club World Cup final last year. Rodri appeared to subtly attempt to usher Trump off the stage before Infantino jogged over to join Trump on the sidelines of the celebrations.

Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino were booed by the crowd as they entered the pitch Image: Lee Smith/REUTERS

Messi on the margins

For much of Sunday’s final, that moment had felt purely a matter of time, as the European champions thoroughly outclassed their South American counterparts.

Just as they did in their impressive semifinal display against France, Spain dominated the ball early and their teenage superstar, Lamine Yamal, came close to opening the scoring in the fifth minute. Seconds later, at the other end of the pitch and the age scale, Lionel Messi was beaten to a through ball by Spanish keeper Unai Simon. It was as close as Messi, 39, got to a significant impact on the game, which may well be his last at a World Cup.

"They were better, to be honest," Messi said postmatch. “We lost the game, and we accept that. That doesn’t mean that we will forget everything we’ve done so far, so I’d like to thank my people, my players and the country."

As the first half wore on in the New York New Jersey stadium, Spain dominated the ball but Argentina held firm, with a smart Emi Martinez save from Spanish striker, Mikel Oyarzabal, as close as either side came before the elongated interval.

Half-time show keeps players waiting

For the first time in World Cup history, a Superbowl style half time show was on the cards. Performers including Madonna, Justin Bieber and BTS took to the pitch with the break extended — contrary to both football convention and FIFA laws — to almost double the standard 15 minutes.

Ferran Torres, on as a substitute, scored the only goal of the game Image: David Ramos/Getty Images/AFP

It wasn’t enough to change the pattern of the game. Spain continued to pass, Argentina continued to scrap, hassle and rely on Martinez to keep Spanish shots at bay.

A red card for midfielder Enzo Fernandez in injury time made Argentina’s task even tougher as the final headed into extra time, as it now has in five of the last six finals. Argentina tired but somehow clung on, with Spain repeatedly wasteful.

Spain keep composure

Surely the South Americans, who had failed to take a single shot in the entire game, couldn’t somehow win this?

But Spain have already proved they won’t panic, with late winners in two of their knockout matches. Indeed, the final bore some resemblance to their tournament opener — a 0-0 draw with Cape Verde. After that, Spain slipped somewhat under the radar for a time, with a lack of cutting edge thought to count them out.

Argentina did not have a shot until deep in to extra time, after falling behind Image: Lee Smith/REUTERS

But as the tournament progressed, Luis de la Fuente’s team have delivered a masterclass in control while sharpening their attacking weapons to win a first World Cup since 2010. Spain’s women are also reigning world champions, winning the tournament in 2023.

"I think that in the end, the goal belonged to 47 million people, not to me or the 26 players here," said the goalscorer, Torres. "I believe that today destiny was written, it was meant for us to win, far from our fans, but we tried to make them feel as close ‌as possible."

World Cup overshadowed by Iran war, Balogun controversy

The final ended a tournament that has offered much from a sporting perspective: the heroics of Cape Verde, the race between Messi and Kylian Mbappe for the tournament — and overall World Cup — top scorer and shocks such as Germany’s exit to Paraguay and Norway toppling Brazil.

But politics has also proved impossible to ignore.

The barring of Somali referee Omar Artan from entering the US added to the sense this was not a World Cup for the whole world. Iran’s treatment, being forced to fly in and out of games and given less preparation time as a result, was a reminder of the conflict between the US and Iran.

Donald Trump’s intervention in the suspension of a red card ban for US striker Folarin Balogun also amplified already loud questions about FIFA corruption.

But, ultimately, the tournament was decided in the same way it always has been. And, on Sunday in New Jersey it was settled, once again, in favor of Spain.

Edited by: Wesley Dockery

World.title: New Bundesliga TV deal in US prioritizes reach over money
World.content:
The Bundesliga has a new home on American screens after Germany's top football league left ESPN. The new deal is a sign of the times.

After six years on ESPN, the Bundesliga has a new home in the United States of America.

A combination of USA Network and Fandango has reportedly struck a deal through the 2030-31 season to be the English-language broadcaster of Germany's top flight in the US. The deal is reportedly worth $20 million (€17.4 million) per year, which is noticeably less than the $34 million per year paid by ESPN.

USA and Fandango are part of Versant, a media company that is trying to develop itself as a home for broadcasting rights below the top leagues of the NFL and NBA. Fandango is predominately an app to buy movie tickets, but Versant is looking to diversify its offering by including live sports. All 300-plus Bundesliga games will air on either channel, with USA requiring a subscription and Fandango being free and ad-supported.

The reaction from US-based Bundesliga fans on social media was mostly negative.

"This will only make the Bundesliga even more obscure," posted @skierpro on X. "Any momentum the league had in the US and growing viewership will be destroyed. The folks in Germany signing this agreement have no idea about the US it seems. They just shot themselves in the foot with this deal."

"This is bad. The simplicity of having every game on ESPN that already has a lot of other sports was perfect. Fandango, a company with nearly no sports streaming experience, may be free, but the games on USA will require an expensive YT TV, Fubo or similar package," posted Corbin Williams on X.

"SAD! USA is OK but Fandango is not a popular streaming app. ESPN was easily accessible. Games on Fandango is going to be like going to the bike shop to buy a BMW," wrote Eric Smith on social media.

New Bundesliga deal a case of less money, but more reach

Some believe the drop in financial return is a sign of the times for the Bundesliga. Others see it as an opportunity.

"From the outside, the new agreement appears to deliver less media-rights income per season but broader distribution, greater discoverability, and a better chance of reaching viewers beyond the Bundesliga's existing fan base. In essence, the reported financial return appears lower, but the potential reach is greater," Dominik Schreyer, a professor of sports economics at Germany's Otto Beisheim School of Management, told DW.

While Schreyer admits that the reported fee being less than the previous deal is disappointing from a business perspective, it is also important to consider its context.

"The DFL is facing a difficult market reality. The media-rights market has become more selective, while competition for audience attention is intensifying. Maximizing the check from each individual cycle may therefore no longer be the only sensible objective," Schreyer said.

"The new distribution model could still prove strategically valuable if its broader reach helps build a larger and more commercially attractive audience over time," he added.

German World Cup winner and former Bayern Munich and Chicago Fire midfielder Bastian Schweinsteiger was one of many popular pundits on ESPN Image: Marco Steinbrenner/DeFodi Images/IMAGO

ESPN's coverage in terms of reporters and commentators was praised by most fans, but the new deal suggests that perhaps it wasn't the ideal place for Germany's top flight.

"My best guess is that the previous model provided insufficient prominence within ESPN's crowded sports portfolio, potentially limiting audience growth. The Bundesliga may now be more important to a partner seeking to establish and differentiate its own live-sports offering in an intensely competitive market, although we cannot know from the outside which considerations ultimately drove the change," Schreyer said.

Is the Bundesliga really growing in America?

"The 2026 World Cup has highlighted the tremendous growth potential of soccer in the US," Robin Austermann, Bundesliga Americas executive vice president, said in a statement. "We've seen that momentum firsthand, with the number of Bundesliga fans in the US growing by 43% over the past five years."

While that may be true, German football's struggle more generally cannot be helping the Bundesliga's position in the market. Bayern Munich have long been dominant domestically, removing both the feeling of competition and suspense in the league. The number of star players isn't high compared to other leagues, and Germany's poor showing at recent World Cups has also weakened the standing of German football globally.

It's clear that the Bundesliga faces an enormous task when it comes to improving its position at the negotiating table for broadcasting deals, much of which is beyond its control. Nevertheless, there is hope that, as mentioned by Austermann, the football momentum provided by the 2026 World Cup in the US, Canada and Mexico can be harnessed to the Bundesliga's advantage.

"It now needs to use prominent scheduling, strong promotion, and localized storytelling to build consumption capital," said Schreyer. "Once viewers discover the product, repeated exposure helps them learn about the clubs, recognize the stars, understand the rivalries and gradually turn occasional viewing into habit, fandom, and ultimately commercial value."

Edited by: Chuck Penfold

World.title: Algeria seeks larger EU energy role amid regional tensions
World.content:
Algeria and Germany agreed to deepen energy ties during President Abdelmadjid Tebboune's recent visit to Berlin. But Algiers is still grappling with tensions at home, over Western Sahara and instability in the Sahel.

For Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune, this week's visit to Berlin marked his first official trip to Germany since he was elected president in 2019. The two-day visit was highlighted in a joint statement with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, in which the two leaders emphasized "the quality of cooperation" between their countries and pledged to deepen long-term energy cooperation.

"Algeria is a central partner for Europe's energy security. Natural gas supplies and cooperation on renewable energies are to be expanded. In the long term, it is about establishing a southern hydrogen corridor — from North Africa to Germany," Cerstin Gammelin, the spokesperson for German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier posted on X on Thursday.

Algeria is home to Africa's second-largest proven natural gas reserves after Nigeria. It is also Africa's largest natural gas producer. On July 2, Algeria's state-owned energy company Sonatrach delivered the first shipment of liquefied natural gas (LNG) directly to Germany's Wilhelmshaven 1 floating LNG import terminal. A direct pipeline to Germany would eliminate the need for liquefaction, LNG shipping and regasification for those volumes. This could reduce transport costs for gas deliveries, as is already the case with Algeria's two existing pipelines to Italy and Spain.

Algeria's domestic demand for gas is increasing while the capacity of the two existing pipelines to southern Europe is limited Image: Billal Bensalem/NurPhoto/picture alliance

"The war in Iran and the disruption of oil exports via the Strait of Hormuz have reinforced Algeria's energy importance," said Alice Gower, director of geopolitics and security at the London-based consulting firm Azure Strategy.

"Although Algeria cannot replace Gulf supplies, its pipeline gas reaches southern Europe without passing through Gulf shipping lanes, offering European governments supply diversification at a time of renewed concern about energy security," she said.

This view is echoed by Hafed Al-Ghwell, director of the North Africa, Mediterranean and the Sahel program at the Washington-based think tank Stimson Center. Al-Ghwell told DW he recently met with Algeria's foreign minister and members of the cabinet.

"You can sense very clearly that there is the political will at the highest level of government that Algeria needs to take advantage of what is happening globally as well as its unique position as a major gas producer," he said.

Algeria at key strategic crossroads

Algeria's value for Europe extends well beyond gas, Gower pointed out. "Algiers offers cooperation on counterterrorism, migration and Mediterranean stability," she told DW.

For years, Algeria has cooperated with European countries on migration management, including returns, border issues and combating smuggling networks.

Moreover, Algiers holds a distinctive diplomatic standing, maintaining relations with both Iran and the United States, as well as the Gulf countries, China and Russia. It is also located at a key strategic crossroads between North Africa and the Sahel region.

"President Tebboune has also placed renewed emphasis on African cooperation, reflecting Algeria's ambition to act as a bridge between North Africa, the Sahel and the wider continent," said Gower.

However, she also noted that this approach is a response to pressure. Algeria is increasingly isolated on the issue of Morocco's claim over the disputed Western Sahara territory. While Algeria supports the local Polisario Front in their quest for independence, Morocco considers Western Sahara part of its territory.

After US President Donald Trump recognized Morocco's sovereignty over the region in 2020, Spain, France and several African nations followed suit.

"Algiers' outreach also aims to preserve its regional influence amid growing Moroccan initiatives," observers wrote in a March analysis of the Institute for Security Studies.

The authors also highlighted that Algeria is a pivotal actor in the Sahel as it shares more than 2,280 kilometers (1,420 miles) of porous borders with Mali and Niger, and faces many of the same challenges, including terrorism, cross-border crime and irregular migration. "Reopening channels of dialogue would serve pressing security, economic and political interests for all."

Algiers has recently sought to repair ties with Mali and Niger. It also supports a political solution for its third large neighboring country, Libya, which remains de facto split in two administrative parts.

Domestic pressure

"A fundamental principle in political science is that foreign policy often reflects domestic politics," Toufik Bougaada, professor of political science at the University of Algiers, told DW.

In his view, this is true for Algeria's situation as well. The Stimson Center's Hafed Al-Ghwell also noted that Algeria is now able to leverage its current stability to address internal dynamics.

"Private sector investment from abroad could help create jobs and specifically address the high level of youth unemployment," he explained.

Algeria continues to grapple with youth unemployment, as international watchdogs sound the alarm over the prosecution of journalists, activists and critics Image: APP/NurPhoto/picture alliance

Algeria has not yet published an official 2026 youth unemployment rate. The latest available World Bank estimate puts youth unemployment at around 29–30%.

Moreover, after the country's longtime ruler Abdelaziz Bouteflika resigned following the Hirak pro-democracy protest movement in 2019, many of the movement's demands for greater political openness remain unmet. Algeria's political system remains controversial until this day.

According to the Bertelsmann Transformation Index 2026, hopes for reform in Algeria after the 2019 Hirak protests have largely faded, with the country having "largely reverted to pre-Arab Spring conditions." The Washington-based think tank Freedom House again classified Algeria as "Not Free" in its Freedom in the World 2026 report .

Recent assessments by Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International describe Algeria as experiencing a continued contraction of civic space. HRW noted that the authorities continued prosecuting journalists, activists and online critics.

Gower therefore remains cautious. "Algeria's expanding geopolitical value has altered the balance of international engagement," she said, adding that "this gives Algeria greater scope to pursue its domestic agenda with reduced external pushback."

Edited by Rainer Sollich

World.title: Germany news: Merz moots Cabinet reshuffle after Spahn exit
World.content:
07/20/2026 July 20, 2026 Bavaria's Markus Söder reportedly pelted with tomato at local event

Bavaria's state premier, Markus Söder, visited celebrations in Bernau am Chiemsee on Sunday, praising rural areas as the "soul of Bavaria."

Söder said in a post online that he had always enjoyed visiting the area, and pledged to develop "tourism, natural protection and the needs of locals in a balanced manner in future."

The conservative CSU leader made no mention, however, of reports on newspaper Bild's website and later on German news agency DPA of a man jumping out a bush and throwing a tomato at him amid the visit.

Bild cited eyewitnesses and a video of the incident. It said that the presumed attacker was swiftly apprehended and that Söder was unhurt.

Bernau am Chiemsee is a small municipality of around 7,000 people on the Chiemsee lake, southeast of Munich and near the Austrian border.

World.title: Spain: Emergency crews battle wildfire north of Madrid
World.content:
More than 25 firefighting planes have been deployed to battle the blaze in central Spain, which has been raging for three days.

Firefighters battled to contain a fast-spreading wildfire north of Spain's capital, Madrid, on Sunday.

The country is still reeling from one of the deadliest wildfires in modern times that killed 13 people and destroyed 7,000 hectares in southern Almeria province earlier this month.

What do we know?

The latest fire started on Thursday in central Spain's Guadalajara province, which includes the Sierra Norte Natural Park.

The area is described as a forest-covered, mountainous region that is home to endangered species, including eagles and wolves.

El Pais newspaper reported that the fire had burned through more than 13,000 hectares by Sunday.

Public broadcaster RTVE reported that the flames had advanced a further 14 kilometers (9 miles) overnight.

More than 500 firefighters and emergency personnel have been deployed to contain the blaze.

Ground crews are also being assisted by 25 firefighting aircraft, officials said.

The fire has scorched 12,000 hectares of land, about 40 miles (80 kilometers) from Madrid Image: Mateo Lanzuela/Europa Press/dpa/picture alliance

Fire crews save 'many lives'

The head of the Castilla-La Mancha regional government, Emiliano Garcia-Page, paid tribute to emergency workers in a post on X, saying they had "managed to save many lives."

Several hundred residents were ordered to evacuate the area.

No casualties have been reported so far.

Man held over suspected arson

A man, accused of starting the fire, was arrested on Thursday, police said, citing a tipoff from neighbors.

Spain remains on high alert for summer wildfires as a severe drought and low humidity affect much of the country at the height of the tourism season.

A major wildfire earlier this month in Almeria province, in the southern Andalucia region, left 13 people dead, including several foreign nationals.

The country remains in shock after revelations that several of the victims were found in burnt-out vehicles, having failed to flee the flames.

Spain: Firefighters battle Andalusia blaze that killed 12 To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Zaragoza fire burns for 4 days

Another wildfire in the northeastern Zaragoza province has been burning since Wednesday, forcing the evacuation of more than a thousand residents.

The regional government warned on Friday evening that the blaze is "far from under control."

However, the head of the Aragon regional government, Jorge Azcon, said Saturday was the "first day we can breathe a sigh of relief," as the fire had been mostly contained.

Since the beginning of the year, wildfires have destroyed more than 80,000 hectares across Spain.

According to the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), that's nearly double the area burned during the same period last year.

Scientists say human-caused climate change is making heatwaves longer, hotter and more frequent — drying out landscapes and fueling more destructive wildfires.

Edited by: Saim Dušan Inayatullah

World.title: Fact check: Spotting AI-generated 'historical' images
World.content:
DW Fact check selected three "historical" videos that aren't real — they're AI. Could you recognize the fake? Here's how to spot it — and why it matters.

In Italy's Pompeii, archaeologists have, for the first time, used artificial intelligence to reconstruct the image of a victim of the volcanic eruption in 79 C.E.

AI is increasingly being used to generate "historical" images as the technology has become widely available, mostly without the consultation of experts. Roland Meyer, a media scholar at the University of Zurich, thinks the trend is no coincidence.

"Through AI, it seems possible to recombine images of the past, generate synthetic images that do not exist but perhaps could have existed, and thus fill perceived or actual gaps in the archive and in the historical record," he said. "To me, however, this seems like a deceptive promise."

AI generators have been known to make mistakes and "hallucinate." DW Fact check explains how to spot AI-created "historical" videos.

#1: Could this video even exist?

Many viral AI‑generated "historical" videos that claim to show the past blur the line between fact and entertainment. They can often be identified by simply asking whether the video could have been made.

"Are we talking about a time when videos already existed, or are we talking about a time when they didn't?" asked historian and AI-specialist Sebastian Kubon.

Sometimes AI-generated content is easy to spot, like in this image, which also carries a label in the bottom left corner Image: TikTok

This video supposedly depicting Pompeii can be discredited on that basis alone.

It also shows clear signs of AI generation. People move in a zombie-like manner, and the woman's appearance looks far more modern than what we know of ancient Rome.

The rise of AI tools has made it easier than ever to create such "historical" images and videos, but experts warn that AI is trained on existing data and will repeat its biases.

"The images of the past generated by AI primarily reproduce the typical patterns, cliches and stereotypes with which that past has been depicted thus far," said Meyer.

"Above all, these are images of our expectations: not a window into the past, but a mirror of our present."

#2: Look for visual clues and check the source

Secondly, a close look at the images themselves and their sources is helpful.

In this video , the camera glides in closer to a group of soldiers holding the US flag, showing their faces as they stare into the distance. It looks more like a Hollywood film than authentic documentary footage.

One soldier in the background glitches unnaturally. The watermark also gives it away: this video was produced by Veo, a generative AI tool.

The video mentioned above is based on the iconic 1945 photograph of US soldiers on Iwo Jima. There is no authentic video footage of this specific moment.

The historic photo of US soldiers raising the flag on the Japanese island of Iwo Jima in 1945 served as the template for an AI video. The AI label is tucked into the watermark, bottom right Image: YouTube

All the experts DW spoke with emphasized the importance of critical source analysis. Where does the image come from, who presents it, for whom and why?

The video's account promises to explore "patriotic stories" and "educational and entertaining content that brings America's story to life." It reveals a handful of similar AI-generated videos.

Images and videos always present a particular perspective, Kubon pointed out.

"They involve a selection of image fragments and audio sources; in essence, they present one perspective on the story. We're too quick to assume that just because something was recorded, it's somehow the truth."

Jürgen Zimmerer, an Africa history professor at the University of Hamburg, warned that visual sources still carry a great deal of authority and have been problematic even before AI.

"Images have always been highly controversial sources. This is evident from the fact that dictatorial regimes, whether Nazi Germany or Stalinist Russia, have also retouched images," he said.

The difference today is the scale at which AI can generate altered and completely fabricated scenes.

#3: Compare with verified historical sources

Look to archives, museums, reputable media or academic experts.

A video showing alleged CCTV footage of the Chernobyl nuclear disaster in 1986 is also AI-generated. Whereas we can find the authentic photograph of Iwo Jima in the US National Archives, no authentic footage exists from this moment in Chernobyl.

'Momemnt of Explosion': glaring typos like this one — or community notes below a post — often hint at whether an image was AI-generated Image: X

Such AI creations raise the question of responsibility.

In comparison to the use of fictional scenes in documentaries, where a director or production team decide how to portray the past, AI pulls from large datasets without understanding of historical context.

"It produces something that looks plausible at first glance, not because it is historically accurate, but because it matches our expectations," Meyer explained.

This is most dangerous when authentic footage does exist, and the video could be real.

Whereas most viewers understand that videos from ancient Rome are fake, large numbers of AI-generated images threaten to replace real documentation of times the technology was present.

Zimmerer emphasized that history is always an approximation. "We approach historical events when there is no original film footage, and when you pretend there is, you make something seem clear that is not actually clear," he said.

So, don't fall for AI-generated historical slop. Dig deeper instead and explore the real past.

World.title: EU ban on destroying unsold clothes takes effect
World.content:
Under new rules to reduce waste, large companies across the European Union can no longer dispose of unsold clothes, accessories and footwear.

A ban on the disposal of unsold clothes and shoes took effect across the European Union on Sunday, in the bloc's latest move to cut waste.

Hundreds of thousands of tons of fashionwear are destroyed every year across the 27-member EU due to damage, old stock and returned online orders.

The new rule is expected to affect large fashion retailers, wholesalers and manufacturers of apparel — only 20% of which are produced in the EU.

What are the new rules?

Under the EU's Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation, large companies with more than 250 employees and over €50 million in net annual turnover are banned from destroying stocks of unsold clothing, accessories and footwear.

Firms must now find ways of selling the products, including via discounts, alternative markets and charity donations.

Unsold clothes can only be destroyed when items are unsafe, damaged, counterfeit or rejected by charities, according to a post on the European Commission's website.

Companies are now required to publish annual reports on the goods they have discarded and keep records for five years.

The regulation, which was approved by Brussels more than two years ago, will be extended to medium-sized firms in 2030.

The EU hopes the disposal ban will help cut CO2 emissions Image: Photoshot/picture alliance

How big is the fashion waste issue?

Concerns about so-called fast fashion — low-cost, lower-quality mass-produced clothing — have grown significantly over the past decade.

According to the European Environment Agency (EEA), around 4% to 9% of unsold textile products are destroyed each year.

The waste has been exacerbated by rapid growth in online shopping and returns.

Across the EU, one in five fashion goods ordered online is later returned to the retailer and not resold.

Combined, this amounts to hundreds of thousands of tons of clothes, accessories and footwear.

The new ban aims to help reduce the impact on the environment, as the incineration of millions of clothes hits efforts to cut greenhouse gas emissions.

EU states are also under pressure to consider waste from raw materials, water, energy and transport in the apparel sector and to encourage more recycling and the reuse of products.

In a recent LinkedIn post, the EEA said the bloc wanted the textile industry to become more sustainable.

"A circular economy — where products are designed to last, and are reused, repaired and recycled — is no longer just a vision, but is being embedded in law through these new legislative measures," the EEA wrote.

The fashion industry has repeatedly defended its tactics, noting that disposal is often cheaper than storing, repairing or discounting the products.

Environment groups hope the ban will cut waste and overproduction Image: Sergieiev/Zoonar/picture alliance

What's the reaction to the ban?

The German Retail Federation (HDE) said consumers would benefit from the ban as more discounted apparel is put on sale through outlets, clearance markets and second-hand channels.

HDE Managing Director Stefan Genth warned, however, that the rule change would be a challenge for many stores.

"Not all unsold goods can be resold or donated easily," he said, due to damaged packaging, high logistics costs, lack of demand or low product values.

Edited by: Saim Dušan Inayatullah

World.title: España habita la eternidad
World.content:
La Roja consigue su segundo Mundial con un gol de Ferran Torres en la prórroga después de reducir a la Argentina de Messi, que no tiró ni una vez hasta el minuto 117

Imposible no recordar Sudáfrica, a Iniesta, a Cesc, la prórroga, el abismo, la gloria. Imposible no verlo en este instante de Ferran Torres que sucedió diez minutos antes, el 106 después de años celebrando la leyenda del 116. Pedri envió una pelota al área, Nico Williams la dejó atrás con la coronilla y Ferran reventó la red y provocó otro estallido inolvidable, la segunda estrella, el segundo título mundial contra la última campeona, a la que redujo casi a la nada. No tiró ni una vez hasta después del gol de la Roja, algo insólito. Ningún equipo se había pasado los 90 minutos de una final sin intentarlo. Ninguno tampoco hasta el 117. El juego de la selección de Luis de la Fuente desmanteló a la Argentina del mítico 10, la abrasó con el juego, la fue pinchando con una sucesión de tiros blandos y la acabó rematando con un zurdazo. Despidió a Messi de los mundiales con una exhibición coral.

ESP España 1 Unai Simón, Pedro Porro, Aymeric Laporte (Eric García, min. 98), Marc Cucurella, Pau Cubarsí, Dani Olmo (Mikel Merino, min. 74), Álex Baena (Nico Williams, min. 74), Rodri (Martín Zubimendi, min. 98), Lamine Yamal, Fabián Ruiz (Pedri, min. 61) y Mikel Oyarzabal (Ferran Torres, min. 61) ARG Argentina 0 Emiliano Martínez, Cristian Romero (Facundo Medina, min. 69), Gonzalo Montiel (Nahuel Molina, min. 57), Nicolás Tagliafico, Lisandro Martínez (Nicolás Otamendi, min. 43), Nico González (Leandro Paredes, min. 45), Alexis Mac Allister, Rodrigo De Paul (Giuliano Simeone, min. 69), Enzo Fernández, Julián Alvarez (Marcos Senesi, min. 101) y Lionel Messi Goles 1-0 min. 105: Ferran Arbitro Slavko Vincic

Tarjetas amarillas Lisandro Martínez (min. 40), Paredes (min. 51), Enzo Fernández (min. 81), Cristian Romero (min. 91), Scaloni (min. 103), Alexis Mac Allister (min. 110) Tarjetas rojas Enzo Fernández (min. 92)

España habita ya la eternidad. Se asomó en Sudáfrica, con la primera versión de un libreto de juego brillante y evolucionó durante algo más de una década a la fórmula prodigiosa con la que ganó la Eurocopa de 2024 y ahora el segundo Mundial. Imposible no recordar Sudáfrica, que llegó también después de un Europeo. La primera estrella es aviso al mundo, sacar la cabeza. La segunda supone instalarse en la eternidad del fútbol.

El entusiasmo por el gol de Ferran, por el juego que parecía inevitable que llevara al título mostró también algo asombroso de un país sumergido en la crispación, pero que ha encontrado algo en lo que consigue ponerse de acuerdo para producir una criatura tan hermosa como este equipo. Para producirlo y para disfrutarlo.

00:40 El gol de Ferran Torres que le ha dado su segundo Mundial a España El gol de Ferrán Torres. Foto: Seth Wenig (AP Photo) | Vídeo: VÍDEO SOLO DISPONIBLE EN ESPAÑA

Lo gigantesco de la ocasión, una final de la Copa del Mundo, no desfiguró a España. Todo lo contrario. Se ha construido para citas de este vuelo estratosférico. Salió a tejer su juego y a asfixiar al rival con lo que le saliera puntada a puntada. Argentina, como casi siempre en el Mundial, parecía querer dejarlo para más adelante, hasta los minutos en los que Messi despierta del letargo. Pero no eran ellos. Era el juego apabullante de la Roja, que los redujo como nadie.

Solo les quedaba aguantar y empezaron levantando las barricadas por el centro. Mac Allister, Enzo Fernández, De Paul y Nico González se apretaban en la zona por la que España ha desplegado sus tramos más brillantes. La encontraron sobrepoblada, pero Dani Olmo maniobra en esos callejones como un escapista que negocia con su propia trampa. Se giró, tiró una pared con Lamine y el extremo del Barcelona se vio en el área ante el Dibu Martínez. Lisandro desvió el tiro y el portero reaccionó con solvencia.

España tocaba, Argentina mantenía los equilibrios, un plan de resistencia que le funciona como a nadie. Porque nadie tiene a Messi, claro, de paseo por la hierba recién regada mientras el resto se desgasta, tomando las medidas del rival para confeccionar el traje en su cabeza. Era pronto para el 10, pero a la defensa española se le distrajo un balón y se encontró encarando a Unai Simón, que aceleró para despejar antes de que lo controlara. No reaccionó a tiempo. No era el momento.

00:19 La entrada a Cubarsí por la que ha sido expulsado Enzo Fernández Foto: JEENAH MOON | Vídeo: VÍDEO SOLO DISPONIBLE EN ESPAÑA

Tampoco era la ruta por la que se esperaba el encuentro. Aunque Unai tuvo que esprintar otra vez para desactivar una carrera de Julián Alvarez. Quedó en nada. Todavía no se había disparado la señal. La refriega iba hacia el otro lado. Argentina ponía cara de que era lo de siempre. Pero no. La señal no llegaba. No había cómo.

España insistía con una partitura en la que Rodri marcaba el tempo y Olmo tocaba la trompeta. El azulgrana pisaba el acelerador y viraba el viento. Buscaban poco a poco más a Lamine Yamal, pero Scaloni le había preparado la vigilancia de dos laterales, Tagliafico y Nico González. Le iban delimitando el territorio, indicándole hasta dónde tenían pensado permitirle avanzar. Que era poco. Enseguida se encontraba con un cuerpo que le chocaba por detrás. Igual que Oyarzabal, desconectado hasta que aparecía por el medio, pero que también iba acumulando rasguños de sus encuentros con los argentinos.

La Roja se enfrentaba a una ardua faena de desbroce, rama a rama, trampa a trampa. Pero este equipo juega con una confianza colosal en la fórmula. Solo se acelera para ir hacia delante. No se demora a contemplarse mientras acumula pases. No se exhibe. Ausculta la fortaleza para introducir una cuña, para abrir una grieta y lanzarse a través de ella.

Argentina acumula horas de resistencia. Esta vez sin respiro, porque no acertaba con los pases. Scaloni maniobró ya en el descanso. Retiró a Nico González y metió a Paredes para seguir vigilando a Lamine, que no encontraba la manera. Messi ni aparecía. El jugador del Barça encaraba, buscaba, pero se perdía en el roce con el que lo trataban.

Después de una hora de paciencia, De la Fuente intervino para seguir empujando. Ferran entró por Oyarzabal y Pedri, por Fabián, buena compañía de Rodri. La música era la misma. Argentina no consideraba necesario nada más. Entraron en el último cuarto, después de la segunda pausa de hidratación, sin haber intentado un solo tiro. Pero con el inconveniente de que se le lesionó otro central, el Cuti Romero.

Lamine consiguió sacar un centro al área, pero Ferran le entregó la pelota de cabeza al Dibu. Pedri encontró un pasadizo desde la frontal, avanzó y tiró muy blando, también al portero. Cubarsí probó desde lejos como contra Bélgica y el Dibu con pudo quedarse con el balón. Salió también Nico Williams y le puso un centro a Laporte, a quien le salió un cabezazo sencillo para el portero.

La respuesta argentina a la tormenta fue insistir en el choque, como vía para llegar a cero a la prórroga. Y ahí les llevó el Dibu con una extraordinaria parada a un tiro libro de Lamine. Se adentraron en ese territorio límite con un futbolista menos por la doble amarilla a Enzo. Su plan entonces era más lija y menos juego. España siguió a lo suyo, con un Nico Williams eléctrico. España ganó con la academia y resistió a la calle, para una segunda estrella eterna.

World.title: Ferran Torres acaba con el “manco” argentino, Dibu Martínez
World.content:
Ferran Torres celebra su gol ante Argentina en la final de la Copa del Mundo.

El audio de esta noticia utiliza una voz sintética generada por Inteligencia Artificial y podría tener algunas inconsistencias.

El delantero español, que inició el Mundial muy discutido, derriba la resistencia del meta albiceleste, autor de 11 paradas, récord en una final desde, al menos, 1966

Ferran Torres era un hombre angustiado el día dos del Mundial. No le cabía la ansiedad en el cuerpo cuando el árbitro fue a consultar al VAR para ver si le validaba un gol ante Arabia Saudí. España ya ganaba 4-0, así que era una cuestión casi exclusivamente personal. Uno de los más discutidos de la Roja necesitaba un refuerzo, un do de pecho que lo impulsara en medio de su propia neblina. Pero no, recibió lo contrario: el colegiado lo dejó sin tanto. Un revés para el azulgrana, muy necesitado de cosas buenas que llevarse a la boca.

Después de haber sido titular en el primer duelo, con Cabo Verde, porque todavía Lamine Yamal no estaba disponible de inicio por la lesión, esa tarde cayó a la suplencia, de donde ya no volvió a salir en el resto del torneo. De la Fuente, eso sí, un entrenador y un tipo de fe, siempre tiró de él como recambio, como en la final. En el minuto 61, sustituyó a un desaparecido Mikel Oyarzabal, perdido en la selva defensiva argentina.

La Albiceleste iba descontando minutos en su aspiración de alcanzar la tanda de penaltis. España nunca se desesperó, siempre esquivó los muchos cepos que dispusieron los argentinos, hasta que un centro al segundo palo de Pedro Porro le abrió el paraíso a Ferran Torres. La pilló por arriba Nico Williams, que la dejó atrás y, con la defensa descuajeringada y con uno menos por la expulsión de Enzo Fernández, apareció como un tiburón Ferran. Tiburón, así se le conoce. Y de eso ejerció. Ya para la eternidad.

“He sido muy criticado en el Mundial, pero el destino estaba escrito. Dios le da las cosas a quien más se lo merece. Nos lo merecíamos. Ha sido un Mundial duro a nivel personal. Soy creyente”, reaccionó el héroe de New Jersey. “Es el gol de 47 millones de españoles. Todas las finales son difíciles, teníamos a Messi enfrente. Pero siempre hemos dependido de nosotros mismos”, analizó a punto de atrapar el trofeo. Si la gloria se juzga por los goles mundialistas: Iniesta y, a su lado, él. Dos carreras, dos estatus y un mismo destino en la cumbre del planeta.

Vista del gol de Ferran. Matt Slocum (AP Photo/Matt Slocum)

Su disparo fue el número 20 de España. Una larga y paciente tarea de demolición que, al fin, pudo fulminó la resistencia argentina personalizada en Dibu Martínez, el portero que murió en unos metros de la orilla después de sostener a su selección. El meta se rompió un dedo de la mano derecha hace dos meses, en el calentamiento de la final de la Europa League que su equipo, el Aston Villa, iba a disputar contra el Friburgo. Le entablillaron la zona, jugó el partido y levantó el título. Unos días más tarde, el seleccionador, Lionel Scaloni, le llamó y le dijo: “Estés como estés, yo te quiero en el equipo en el Mundial”, contó este viernes el guardameta. Y allí apareció, lesionado y hecho una incógnita.

“Hasta dos días antes del primer partido del Mundial [contra Argelia], me tiraba con una mano. Parecía manco”, desveló en la previa de la final. A la cita cumbre con España llegó, de hecho, todavía con dolores. Había consultado con varios especialistas y todos le habían dicho que debía operarse y estar de baja unas seis semanas, pero eso implicaba la fase de grupos, algo que se negó a aceptar. Así que tiró hacia adelante, hizo contención de daños y confío en que el tiempo fuera soldando la fractura. Scaloni también cumplió y le dio cuerda desde el día uno de torneo. No falló ningún día y menos en la final.
