World.title: Spain beat Argentina to win World Cup
World.content:
East Rutherford – Ferran Torres scored the only goal of the game on Sunday as Spain beat 10-man Argentina 1-0 after extra-time to win their second World Cup.

The European champions dominated the match at the MetLife Stadium but struggled to find a breakthrough against the streetwise defending champions.

Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez made a string of saves to deny Spain, but the match changed complexion in second-half stoppage-time when midfielder Enzo Fernandez was sent off for a second yellow card after a reckless tackle on Pau Cubarsi.

Extra-time followed a familiar pattern, with Spain probing for the opening goal against a deep-lying Argentina.

The breakthrough eventually came in the early moments of the second period of extra-time when substitute Torres finished crisply following a brilliant knock-back by Nico Williams.

Luis de la Fuente’s Spain conceded just one goal in seven matches on their way to the final, suffocating opponents with their slick possession game.

Lionel Messi’s Argentina battled their way through the knockout rounds, coming back from the dead against Egypt and recovering from a goal down to beat England in the semi-finals.

World.title: US strikes Iran after troops killed in Iraq and Jordan
World.content:
Tehran – The United States and Iran traded missiles and airstrikes on Sunday as Washington sought to \”punish\” Tehran for the US military’s first losses since open hostilities in the Middle East war resumed.

A preliminary deal aimed at ending the war has collapsed as the foes fight to break a deadlock over the Strait of Hormuz, a waterway key to the world’s oil supply.

Iran said it targeted two US bases in Kuwait in response to more than a week of intensifying attacks, which Tehran says have hit transport and infrastructure sites, including an under-construction nuclear power plant.

Jordan also reported intercepting missiles, a day after the US military said two service members were killed there Friday and another had gone missing in action as they \”defended against Iranian ballistic missile and drone attacks\”.

US Central Command announced on Sunday that a service member died in northern Iraq during the controlled detonation of an unexploded ordnance from a downed Iranian drone.

The US military carried out an eighth consecutive night of strikes against Iran to \”swiftly punish Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces who launched attacks against American service members\”, Central Command said.

Saturday’s death brought to 17 the confirmed number of American military fatalities since the US and Israel launched the war with a wave of strikes on Iranian targets on February 28.

The Atomic Energy Organization of Iran said the United States had attacked the unfinished Darkhovin nuclear power plant in the country’s southwest, calling it \”an aggressive and brutal act contrary to international law\”.

The UN’s nuclear watchdog said it was looking into the report, noting the plant \”contained no nuclear material when last visited by the IAEA\”.

Nonetheless, IAEA director Rafael Grossi reiterated his \”call for military restraint in the vicinity of all nuclear-related sites\”, the agency said in a post on X.

Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi meanwhile said on X that Tehran \”will take appropriate action to defend its national interests and security.\”

– ‘Treacherous’ attacks –

After air raid sirens sounded in Jordan, Israel’s military said its forces along with Jordan’s had intercepted an Iranian missile heading towards the Jordanian port city of Aqaba — just across the border from Israel’s resort town of Eilat.

Iran did not immediately claim the attack, but the US embassy in Amman had earlier warned its citizens of a \”specific and credible threat\” targeting Aqaba’s port and airport.

\”If Iran fires missiles at Israel, we will attack them with full force,\” Defence Minister Israel Katz said, adding it was \”prepared for both defensive and offensive\” action against Tehran if need be.

Jordan later said it had summoned Iran’s charge d’affaires to strongly protest the \”continuation of brutal and unjustified Iranian acts of aggression targeting the Kingdom’s territory\”.

In the Gulf, which has borne the brunt of Iran’s retaliatory attacks, Kuwait’s electricity ministry said a power and water plant was attacked for a second consecutive day, causing a fire.

Bahrain’s military also said its air defences \”confronted, intercepted, and destroyed a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks\”, accusing Iran of targeting civilians.

– American ‘mischief’ –

The renewed violence was initially sparked by Iranian attacks on ships in the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

Iran closed the conduit for oil and gas shipments after the war broke out, and control over it has become leverage in its negotiations with Washington, which has reimposed its own blockade on Iranian ports.

On Sunday, the Revolutionary Guards said two ships attempting to transit the strait were stopped.

\”Four violating ships, with the mischief and support of American terrorists…intended to disrupt and exit the Strait of Hormuz via an unsafe route, two of which had an accident and were stopped in place,\” the Guards said, adding that the other two ships abandoned their journey.

Iran’s health ministry said Friday that 50 people had been killed in the recent fighting and more than 500 hurt.

Hope for a political settlement to the war has dimmed, though mediators have attempted to bring both sides back to the negotiating table.

Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who took over after his father was killed in the opening salvo of US-Israeli strikes, vowed to teach the Americans \”unforgettable lessons\” in a statement Saturday.

And Iran’s central military commander, Ali Abdollahi, warned that further US aggression would face a \”decisive and devastating response\”, according to a statement carried by state television on Sunday.

World.title: Madonna, Shakira, Bieber and The Muppets light up World Cup half-time show
World.content:
East Rutherford – Musical headliners Madonna, Shakira, Justin Bieber, BTS and Coldplay were joined by Brazilian soccer icons and \”Ted Lasso\” actors in a spectacular first-ever World Cup final halftime show on Sunday.

The star-packed, Super Bowl-style extravaganza — a first for soccer’s showpiece event — also featured a tribute to football icon Pele, and a rendition of \”Seven Nation Army\” led by Gustavo Dudamel and featuring musicians from the US, Venezuela and Iran.

\”Sesame Street\” and \”The Muppets\” characters joined Coldplay and a New York elementary school choir to close out a performance designed to raise money for the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, which promotes access to sport for under-privileged children.

The 12-minute performance meant the total halftime break in the match between Spain and Argentina lasted 27 minutes.

– Largest since Live Aid? –

Organizers had billed the halftime show as \”the single largest gathering of artists united for a cause since Live Aid,\” and \”the most-watched 11 minutes of broadcast music performance in history\”.

FIFA chief Gianni Infantino predicted \”a couple of billion\” people would tune in.

The extended interruption to soccer’s most important game had drawn some criticism over the potential impact on players’ performance.

While highly unusual for soccer, the show was slightly shorter than most recent Super Bowl halftime performances, which have typically been around 13-14 minutes long.

The crowd erupted with a roar as the show began with Madonna being transported through tunnels beneath the MetLife Stadium on a dune buggy driven by Brazil soccer legends Ronaldo and Ronaldinho.

Her performance of \”Music\” led to an orchestra featuring the New York Philharmonic, Venezuela’s Simon Bolivar Symphony Orchestra and Iranian violinist Bijan Mortazavi performing the White Stripes’ \”Seven Nation Army\” — a rock hit that has become a global US soccer stadium staple.

Footage of the Norway fans’ \”Viking row\” celebration from this tournament led into K-pop sensation BTS performing their smash hit \”Dynamite,\” rewritten with soccer-specific lyrics, before \”Ted Lasso\” star Jason Sudeikis and his \”Coach Beard\” sidekick Brendan Hunt made a surprise appearance.

They introduced Canadian pop megastar Bieber, who performed an emotional, World Cup-tailored version of \”Everything Hallelujah,\” before Shakira and Nigerian singer Burna Boy ramped the energy back up with this World Cup’s anthem, \”Dai Dai,\” accompanied by Ugandan dancers.

– ‘Driving force’ –

Ggiant screens showed footage of Brazil’s late soccer icon Pele from 1977, addressing the crowd at the old Giants Stadium on this same New Jersey site following his final professional game. Pele passed away in 2022, months after the last World Cup.

PS22 Chorus, a New York school choir that has gone viral globally with YouTube covers of popular hits, closed out the show, with Coldplay — whose singer Chris Martin curated the entire performance — and characters from \”The Muppets\” and \”Sesame Street.\”

The FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund was described by organizers as the \”driving force\” behind the halftime show.

It disburses cash to community groups that provide education and sport to under-priviliged children in countries from Ghana and South Africa to France and the United Kingdom.

The fund aims to raise $100 million. It had passed $60 million before the show, including a $1 donation from every World Cup ticket sold, plus contributions from corporations, nation states and private donors.

FIFA has already announced 58 groups that will receive grants, reaching 400,000 children worldwide.

Even before the game, a parade of stars took the microphone to whip up the crowd.

Post Malone headlined a closing ceremony, and Tom Cruise delivered a monologue about football unifying the world — but was largely drowned out in the stadium by singing fans.

Robbie Williams, Nicole Scherzinger and Jennifer Hudson were among further A-list performers.

World.title: US soldier killed in Iraq while dismantling Iranian attack drone
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com)—A US service member was killed and another injured in northern Iraq while disposing of explosive ordnance from a crashed Iranian one-way attack drone, the US military announced on Sunday.

The soldier was killed on July 18 during a controlled explosion of unexploded explosives from the drone, while the second service member had a minor injury and is being treated, according to US Central Command (CENTCOM).

The event occurs as Iraq strives to convince international investors that improved security and economic reforms are rebuilding trust after decades of strife, despite regional tensions spilling into Iraqi territory.

During a recent visit to Washington, Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s government signed a series of agreements with US companies and financial institutions on energy, infrastructure, aviation, and banking as part of Baghdad’s larger effort to diversify its economy and attract foreign investment.

The latest incident highlights the security threats that continue to impede Iraq’s recovery, with strikes utilizing Iranian drones and Iran-backed armed groups disturbing peace, resulting in lives and injuries, and threatening to dissuade foreign investment.

Separately, CENTCOM said that two US service members died as a result of an Iranian strike in Jordan on July 17 and that military troops subsequently discovered unidentifiable remains suspected to be those of a third service member who had been reported missing.

An investigation to confirm the remains is continuing.

CENTCOM said that it was concealing the identity of the deceased and missing service men out of respect for their families until the notification procedure was completed.

Following years of conflict, Iraq has increasingly sought to position itself as a stable destination for international business.

However, recurring regional hostilities have repeatedly exposed the country’s vulnerability to broader tensions between Iran and the United States, complicating Baghdad’s efforts to restore normalcy and sustain its economic recovery.

World.title: PM Al Zaidi carries Trump message to Iran; Tehran declines Supreme Leader meeting
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Well-informed sources have disclosed to the Kuwaiti newspaper Al-Jarida, that Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi is carrying a verbal message from U.S. President Donald Trump addressed to the Iranian leadership. This message, which al-Zaidi received during his recent official visit to Washington, comes as the U.S.–Iran confrontation edges closer to a broader war amid ongoing regional military escalation.

The sources from the Iranian Supreme National Security Council explained that the Iraqi Prime Minister’s stopover in the Qatari capital of Doha on Sunday was specifically aimed at coordinating the core substance of this message with the Qatari side. Baghdad is seeking to evaluate the possibility of transforming this verbal message into a tangible Iraqi initiative that works in tandem with current mediation tracks led by Qatar and Pakistan to de-escalate regional tensions.

Diplomatic Tracks and the Backstage of the Upcoming Tehran Visit

Timeline of the Visit: Prime Minister al-Zaidi’s state visit to Tehran is officially scheduled for next Thursday, though Baghdad has expressed full readiness to move the date forward if regional developments demand it.

Iraqi Request for a Supreme Leader Meeting: The Iraqi delegation expressed a strong desire to leverage the special bilateral relationship between the two neighbors to make al-Zaidi the first foreign official to meet with Iran’s new Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei.

Iranian Refusal Based on Security Protocol: The Iranian source completely ruled out the possibility of such a meeting, confirming that the Iraqi delegation was officially notified of the decision. The refusal was attributed to strict Iranian security anxieties regarding the potential exposure of the new Supreme Leader’s secure location, given that he has remained completely out of public sight since the outbreak of the war on Iran last February. Tehran noted that the standard official protocols and security footprint required for hosting a foreign prime minister would pose an unacceptable security risk.

Alternative Intelligence Claims: In contrast to Tehran’s official justification, regional and Hebrew media outlets quoted an Israeli security source claiming that Mojtaba Khamenei is not actually inside Iranian territory. The intelligence source alleged that the strategic messages attributed to the Supreme Leader are entirely drafted by Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Commander Ahmed Vahidi.

On the domestic front in Tehran, former Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif is spearheading a political narrative that encourages the Iranian leadership to maintain its current stance and resist external pressures until the conclusion of the American elections. Zarif based his strategic view on recent communications he allegedly received from several U.S. Democratic politicians. According to his account, these American figures suggested that a potential electoral setback for Trump in November could push Congress to take decisive legislative action to halt the war.

Conversely, the governing domestic alliance uniting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf remains firmly committed to pursuing direct diplomatic understandings with Washington to end the crisis. The position of this moderate faction was recently reinforced following a directive issued by the Supreme Leader, which ordered an immediate halt to internal political public criticism of state officials.

This directive was translated into immediate action on the ground, as strict orders were handed down to hardline, ultra-conservative media outlets to completely cease their coordinated media campaigns against Pezeshkian and Qalibaf. The state warned that any violation of this freeze would result in severe regulatory and legal penalties, up to and including the permanent revocation of corporate media broadcasting licenses.

World.title: Iraq’s Integrity Commission arrests electricity official over 4.5B IQD cable theft
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Federal Integrity Commission announced on Sunday, July 19, 2026, the arrest of a senior official within the Baghdad Electricity Distribution Company for the embezzlement and illicit seizure of state-owned electrical infrastructure materials valued at nearly 4.5 billion Iraqi Dinars (IQD).

According to an official statement released by the commission, a specialized investigative and auditing task force was deployed directly to the Ministry of Electricity to audit regional inventory systems.

The investigation revealed that the head of the warehouses for the Rusafa distribution branch had illegally seized high-voltage electrical cables totaling 4,406,000,000 IQD in value. The commission noted that the primary suspect executed the embezzlement scheme in direct cooperation with two civilian vehicle owners who assisted in transporting the stolen state property out of the facility.

The arrest was carried out under a formal judicial warrant issued by the Judge of the Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Court, in accordance with the statutory provisions of Article 315 of the Iraqi Penal Code, which strictly penalizes the embezzlement of public funds by state employees.

A formal seizure record was legally documented, and the primary suspect was presented before the competent investigative judge, who subsequently ordered him to be remanded in custody pending further judicial proceedings.

Investigation Brief: Rusafa Grid Embezzlement Case

World.title: Influencer Andrew Tate and brother arrested in Miami
World.content:
Washington – Radical social media influencer Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan were on Sunday in custody in the US, officials said, as Britain seeks their extradition to face new charges of rape, sex trafficking and assault.

Karena Thomas, assistant chief constable of the UK’s Bedfordshire Police, said the pair had been detained \”pending ongoing legal proceedings.\”

The US Marshals Service confirmed the arrests.

US news outlet TMZ posted video of law enforcement officers placing the self-professed misogynist and his younger sibling in handcuffs and escorting them into waiting vehicles in Miami on Saturday.

Asked by an onlooker if he had something to say, Tristan Tate did not respond, the footage posted on X showed.

UK prosecutors, who are now due to seek the brothers’ extradition, said the arrests came after they brought forward 38 further charges against the pair.

The Tate brothers now face 59 charges in total — 42 against Andrew and 17 against Tristan, British authorities said on Sunday.

\”We have decided to prosecute Andrew and Tristan Tate for further offences including rape, arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation and offences relating to indecent images of a child,\” Malcolm McHaffie, head of the UK’s Crown Prosecution Service’s (CPS) Special Crime Division, said in a statement.

\”The CPS has requested the extradition of the Tates from the US,\” he said, adding that the latest charges stem from receipt of new evidence from Bedfordshire Police that brings the total number of alleged victims in the Tates case to seven.

Earlier this year, police in Hertfordshire, north of London, said they were reopening a probe into rape and sexual assault allegations made by women against Andrew Tate between 2014 and 2015.

They also face separate rape and human trafficking allegations brought by different women and investigated by Bedfordshire Police, which covers their hometown of Luton, also north of London.

\”There is no place for male violence against women and girls, and we will continue to work tirelessly to support victims and investigate all reports made to us,\” Bedfordshire Police’s Thomas added.

– ‘Face justice’ –

The Tate brothers are also accused of tax evasion and money laundering in the UK.

Their attorney, Joseph McBride, said in a press release that the brothers \”are innocent.\”

\”We are confident that once a competent judge sees the facts, and once the Department of Justice confronts this egregious abuse of its own authority, Andrew and Tristan Tate will walk free,\” McBride said.

The Tates are dual British-US citizens who have been avid supporters of US President Donald Trump.

Lawyer Matt Jury, of McCue Jury & Partners who represent four alleged British victims of Andrew Tate, said Tate was \”now facing the real prospect of extradition to the UK after years of public campaigning by the four British women I represent.

\”They have spent years fighting for action to be taken, and I now urge the authorities to ensure this case proceeds as quickly as possible.

\”Andrew and Tristan Tate are accused of some of the most serious offences, including multiple counts of rape and human trafficking. It is time they face justice,\” he was quoted by the PA news agency as saying.

In March 2025, the US state of Florida launched a criminal investigation against them. The status of that investigation is unclear.

Andrew Tate is one of the most prominent proponents of the so-called \”manosphere\” network of communities, many of them online, that focus on traditional masculinity, anti-feminism, and self-improvement.

He promotes his divisive views, often incorporating alpha-male and aggressively misogynistic themes, to millions on social media including 10.8 million followers on X.

In Romania, where they have been based in recent years, the Tates face allegations of trafficking minors, sexual intercourse with a minor and money laundering.

World.title: Iraqi dinar declines against US dollar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar declined on Sunday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly declined in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,520 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,526 Iraqi dinars on Sunday’s morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,525 Iraqi dinars and 1,515 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate dropped, fluctuating between 1,523 and 1,522.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Congress demands independent probe into donation chori
World.content: NEW DELHI: Leaders of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi Sunday shot off a letter to PM Narendra Modi demanding an independent probe into the Ram temple donation issue and warning that his govt's credibility depends on its swift action - putting the controversy high on the opposition's agenda for Parliament's monsoon session that may lead to confrontation with govt.Also, with Cockroach Janta Party and activist Sonam Wangchuk planned to march to Parliament Monday over paper leaks and to demand the resignation of the education minister, many opposition parties have supported the protest, and are likely to turn up at Jantar Mantar for the Parliament gherao.The twin issues, on which the opposition is seeking a discussion, are likely to dominate the first week of the session, with BJP in the crosshairs. Congress believes these controversies can hurt the governing party politically as they affect a large segment of Indian population and youth.Kharge and Rahul told Modi that he had announced the formation of Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Teerth Kshetra in Parliament, and its members appointed by Centre are closely associated with RSS, VHP and affiliates, while its "disgraced former general secretary" is "your close associate".They said in the letter,"Your silence now in the face of such a crime is unacceptable."The Congress duo said the findings of the independent probe and the trust's accounts should be made public so that every devotee knows how their offerings have been used.There is a consensus among opposition parties that govt should discuss the issue in Parliament, with SP's Dharmendra Yadav, RSP's NK Premachandran, CPI's Sandosh Kumar stressing the demand in the all-party meeting with govt.Ahead of the session, govt's decision to break up Wangchuk's hunger strike through police action has led to the opposition condemning the Modi govt. -

World.title: Stormy session ahead as opposition flags temple row, NEET, E20
World.content:
Cong Can Raise Demand, Canât Force Govt: Rijiju

Govt lists 8-bill agenda, silent on delimitation

New Delhi: Opposition on Sunday pushed for discussion in Parliament over embezzlement of donations at Ram temple, NEET paper leak coupled with the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar, and the row over E20 petrol, signalling a tumultuous monsoon session from Monday, as govt cautioned its rivals that any disruption of the legislature is bound to cost them politically.Amid indications that govt is unlikely to allow its rivals to raise in Parliament the theft of temple donations, parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju called for consultation instead of a âmy way or highwayâ attitude over the issues to be picked up for debate.âCongress has every right to raise its demand, but it canât force govt,â he said, after Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge wrote to PM Modi, timing their demand for probe and accountability with the sessionâs start, as several opposition MPs, including SPâs Dharmendra Yadav, raised the issue in an all-party meet led by defence minister Rajnath Singh and attended by 58 MPs of 40 parties.While listing its agenda of eight bills, govt made no mention of its likely move to revive the constitution amendment bill for raising the strength of Lok Sabha and rolling out one-third reservation for women from 2029.Rijiju, though, told reporters later that govt could bring a new item in accordance with the rules after discussing it in the business advisory committee (BAC) during the session, a common practice.He said people had seen that political parties that disrupt Parliament and do not allow discussion end up paying a price, an apparent reminder to BJPâs rivals of their poor show in a string of assembly polls, with once-formidable regional parties Trinamool Congress and DMK losing in West Bengal and Tamil Nadu, respectively.With several opposition members raising the NEET-UG paper leak and questioning govt for not engaging with protesters at Jantar Mantar, RSP MP N K Premachandran pushed for a structured debate over the issue, saying paper leaks affect students in huge numbers.As some opposition MPs spoke of the recent fuel price hike, BJP ally and JDU MP Sanjay Jha sought a debate on the West Asia crisis as he credited govt for its energy management, saying it had ensured minimal rise in oil and gas prices compared with other countries and expanded supply for India through alternative sources. India handled its adverse impacts deftly, he said.

World.title: Opposition protests invite to TMC rebels to all-party meeting
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In solidarity with the Mamata Banerjee-headed Trinamool Congress, opposition parties on Sunday staged a rare walkout from the all-party meeting to protest the govtâs invite to its breakaway faction, even as both warring groups took potshots at one another, foretelling a fiery session of Parliament from Monday.

Govt, however, defended its decision, asserting that it cannot deny space to the faction of 20 MPs who have approached Speaker Om Birla for recognising their merger with Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) and have already been allotted separate seats in Lok Sabha.

âIt is govtâs duty to invite every group,â parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju told reporters. Playing down the walkout, he said it was only for a brief period as opposition parties rejoined the meeting soon.

Facing disintegration and an existential crisis, TMC has leaned on other opposition parties, including Congress, which used to get short shrift from the party in Parliament when Mamata was West Bengalâs chief minister, to strengthen its cause.

John Brittas of CPM, which has been a bitter critic of Mamata, said they supported the party in the walkout in the interests of parliamentary democracy which is under âattackâ from BJP.





As Mahua Moitra, who is among the eight Lok Sabha MPs siding with Mamata, called the majority bloc of 20 MPs âtraitorsâ and demanded their disqualification, Sudip Bandyopadhyay, the chosen leader of breakaway faction, retorted that a âsmallâ party with only eight MPs no longer deserves front row seating in House.

Mahua was joined by members of other opposition parties as she slammed the invitation to Sudip as the NCPI leader and to Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar as its chief whip and claimed that they cannot be recognised under anti-defection law. Only original party can merge with another party, she added.

World.title: Well-oiled labour supply chain facilitating illegal infiltration of Bangladeshis
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A large majority of Bangladeshi illegal immigrants who sneak into India are not here to organically âexploreâ economic opportunities; they cross over as part of a well-oiled labour supply chain, with Indian employers in states far from the border relying on headhunting touts in Bangladesh for cheap labour.

The âjobs for illegal immigrantsâ eco-system has touts at every stage â facilitating infiltration, transportation to job sites and arranging forged documentation before settling them into jobs across sectors such as textile manufacturing, construction and pharmaceuticals.

âItâs an organised eco-system that comprises Bangladeshi recruitment touts who, based on requirements of Indian employers for cheap labour, identify unemployed Bangladeshis seeking low-paid, unskilled jobs in India.

Every step, from their illegal entry into India to reaching their job locations, is planned well in advance,â a senior Assam govt official told TOI.

The official said infiltration guides help the selected Bangladeshis cross over, mostly through Meghalaya, Tripura and West Bengal. Agents on the Indian side arrange their transit to Assam and onward train journeys from Guwahati to job locations across the country.





Local touts help them secure forged documents like Aadhaar before another set of agents hand them over to Indian employers willing to hire them at wages lower than those payable to Indians.

Assam, which recently busted one such tout network transporting illegal immigrants from Guwahati railway station to Tamil Nadu to work in a textile factory, leading to 34 arrests, raised the issue at the all-India conference of SPs of border districts chaired by home minister Amit Shah on July 9.

The state sought a legal framework to hold Indian employers exploiting the Bangladeshi illegal immigration network accountable.

Intelligence sources said Bangladeshi headhunters work on labour demand conveyed by agents linked to Indian employers. The network also arranges forged Aadhaar and PAN cards in destination states, enabling illegal immigrants to register as workers and move between work sites.

âArmed with the same documents, many went on to project themselves as Indian citizens and even enrolled as voters. Special intensive revision (SIR), however, may have cut their dream run short by requiring proof of their parentsâ or relativesâ presence in the 2002 rolls,â a police officer told TOI.

World.title: Even as fertility rates drop, young still aspire to partnership, parenthood, shows UN report
World.content: NEW DELHI: A first-of-its-kind survey of young adults (aged 18-39) across 73 countries, including India, by United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) shows that even as much of the worldâs marriage rates have declined and fertility has fallen to historically low levels, young people are not turning away from relationships or family life. Marriage, it says, remains âa common ideal relationshipâ arrangement among surveyed young adults.The report highlights that across countries â with very different demographic realities â many continue to aspire to partnership and parenthood, but say their decisions are increasingly shaped by financial security, stable employment, housing, gender equality and confidence in the future.UNFPAâs âLives, Choices and Futures â Demographic Futures Surveyâ 2026â gathered perspectives of more than 1,08,000 internet connected young adults, including 1,722 respondents in India.More than two thirds of respondents selected an ideal relationship and living arrangement that includes marriage â 36% before living together and 34% after a period of cohabitation. The survey says 16% reported remaining single as their preferred living arrangement.Its findings gain significance, as across much of the world partnership formation is occurring later, marriage rates have declined and fertility has fallen to historically low levels.âTwo thirds of the worldâs population now lives in a country or area where the total fertility rate is below 2.1 children per woman â the level commonly associated with the population size remaining stable over time,â the survey says.Among respondents aged 25â39, who ideally wish to marry or live with a partner, a quarter are currently single and not dating. The proportion is higher among male respondents (30% than among female respondents (19%).Financial security is the highest-rated consideration for partnership formation, cited as important by 81% of respondents. It turns out that economic and housing constraints constitute the most commonly reported category of barrier to partnership, rated important by 57%.The survey finds that among respondents â currently seeking a partner â personal networks, school or work environments, and online platforms are the most commonly reported channels for meeting potential partners, each reported by approximately one third of respondents. Overall the survey says more than 40% of respondents report spending over two hours a day on social media or the Internet for entertainment, making it the most time-intensive form of online activity examined.In India, while more than eight in 10 respondents (83%) said they feel positive or very positive about the future, nearly half of those surveyed (47%) said they are very worried about conflict, economic insecurity and inequality.While across most regional groupings of countries, two children is the most commonly reported ideal family size, the mean number of children reported by respondents aged 35â39 is lower than the mean ideal number of children reported by respondents aged 18â39.For instance, in the case of India, women aged 18-39 reported an ideal family size of 2.1 children, compared with an average of one child among women aged 35-39. Men reported an ideal family size of 2.2 children, compared with an average of 1.1 children among men aged 35-39.Parenthood is part of the future plans of most surveyed in India. Among respondents aged 35-39 in India who do not currently have children, nearly 85% said they would ideally like to become parents.

World.title: Less than half of 483 Lok Sabha MPs attended 90-100% of sittings in Parliament’s budget session, shows analysis
World.content:
NEW DELHI: As parties gear-up for taking up a wide range of issues during Parliamentâs monsoon session â expected to be fiery in light of Ram temple and NEET-UG paper leak issues â the presence of MPs in both Houses is most crucial.

An analysis of attendance record of the previous budget session, which ended in April, by NGO Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative shows that it is the smaller parties â with a handful of MPs â that have the highest average attendance record figures.

Overall in Lok Sabha, as many as 101 MPs had signed the attendance register for all 31 sittings of the budget session â less than a quarter, or just about 21% of the 483 MPs whose attendance record was publicly available.

In terms of average attendance record of parties in LS, RLP â that has one MP (Hanuman Beniwal from Nagaur â and RLD â that has two MPs (Chandan Chauhan from Bijnor and Rajkumar Sangwan from Baghpat â registered 100% attendance record for all 31 sittings. CPI(ML-L) stood second â with two of its MPs attending 30 out of the 31 sittings â as did Zoram Peopleâs Movement with its lone MPs. Samajwadi Party took third position â with 37 of its MPs averaging attendance of 28.43 days.





Overall less than one half (45.7%) of the 483 LS members had attended between 90-100% of the sittings or at least signed the attendance register. The report examines the attendance record as available on the website of both Houses for the budget session to spot political party-wise trends and patterns.

The single-largest party in LS, BJP (with details of 191 members available) averaged only 26.46 sittings per MP. Congress â single-largest party in opposition â averaged only 23.13 sittings (with details of 97 MPs available).

Among regional political parties with more than 20 MPs during the budget session, TMC averaged only 15 sittings and DMK with 22 MPs even lesser with 14.64 sittings.

In Rajya Sabha, 119 MPs â less than 46.6% of 255 MPs had attended between 90-100% of the sittings or at least signed the attendance register for those many days.

The top 10 political parties clocking the highest percentage of attendance are regional parties. DMDK with its lone MP (LK Sudhish) is the only one who recorded 100% attendance, followed by J&K-NC with three MPs clocking an average of 94.62%. MPs from JDS, MNF, BJD, SP, NPP and SS all recorded an average of more than 90% attendance.

Despite being the largest party in the House, BJP recorded an average attendance of only 84.39% followed by Congress recording 80.66%, the report stated.

World.title: 'Rise in instability in Iran': Indian embassy sounds alarm; urges people to leave, postpone travel
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Indian Embassy in Iran on Sunday issued a revised travel advisory, urging Indian nationals to postpone all travel to the country.

It also advised Indians already in Tehran to consider temporarily leaving the country using available commercial flights, as the security situation continues to deteriorate amid the escalating conflict in the Middle East.

The advisory comes as military hostilities between the United States and Iran have intensified, with fresh strikes, retaliatory attacks and growing concerns over the security situation across the region.

In its advisory, the embassy said, "The recent days have seen an increase in levels of instability and conflict in Iran."

It advised Indian nationals planning to visit Iran 'for any purpose' to postpone their travel until the security environment improves.

The embassy also urged Indians already in Iran to 'consider temporarily exiting Iran, using available flight options.'

For those choosing to remain in the country, the mission advised exercising the highest level of caution, closely monitoring local developments and avoiding areas witnessing increased military activity, particularly along Iran's southern coast.

"Indian nationals who choose to remain in Iran should exercise the highest possible level of caution.





They should carefully monitor the news to maintain full situational awareness, and should avoid locations seeing higher levels of military activity such as those along the southern coast of the country. Instructions issued by local authorities should be complied with carefully," the advisory read.

The embassy also asked all Indian nationals in Iran who have not yet registered with the mission to do so immediately and regularly follow its official website and social media channels for further updates.

The advisory was issued as the conflict between the United States and Iran escalated further on Sunday.

According to Iranian authorities, the United States carried out fresh strikes on the under-construction Darkhovin nuclear power plant and other military targets, while the US Central Command (CENTCOM) said it targeted Iranian coastal surveillance systems, air defence networks, maritime assets and missile and drone facilities.

Iran, meanwhile, announced retaliatory drone attacks against two US military installations in Kuwait and claimed to have intercepted a US MQ-9 drone over Ahvaz. It also warned that the Strait of Hormuz remained under the control of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), amid heightened tensions over maritime security.

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said it was investigating reports of the attack on the Darkhovin nuclear facility and added that the site contained no nuclear material during its last inspection. The UN nuclear watchdog said the reported strike was not believed to pose any radiological risk but reiterated its call for military restraint around nuclear-related sites.

The latest escalation has raised fresh international concern over the widening conflict in the Middle East as the war completes nearly five months.

World.title: 'He intends to continue the fast': Sonam Wangchuk's wife vows to lead Parliament march
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Educationalist and climate activist

's wife, Gitanjali J Angmo on Sunday said that she would lead the planned march to Parliament on Monday to represent her husband along with the students and parents protesting against the alleged NEET-UG paper leak, asserting that Wangchuk intends to continue his indefinite hunger strike.

Her remarks came after the Delhi high court declined to grant urgent interim relief seeking Wangchuk's immediate discharge from Safdarjung Hospital and his transfer to a private hospital.

Speaking to reporters outside the Delhi high court, Angmo said she would participate in the march on behalf of Wangchuk, who was shifted to Safdarjung Hospital on Saturday after being removed from the protest site at Jantar Mantar.

"I will definitely represent him in tomorrow's protest. We filed an urgent petition today because, had we been allowed to shift today, we could have gone to Medanta and then arrived at the protest site by tomorrow morning. But we knew they wouldn't allow that. I am ready to represent Sonam Wangchuk, and I will definitely join the march tomorrow," she said.

Appealing to those planning to join the march, Angmo urged protesters to remain peaceful and vigilant.





"To all the students and parents coming to join the march tomorrow, I would say: keep two things in mind. First, let us conduct this march in a completely peaceful manner. Second, remain vigilant against nefarious elements who might try to disrupt it. Let us stay alert and avoid falling into their traps. Attempts might be made to incite trouble or give the event a different complexion," she said.

She also said Wangchuk remained determined to continue his fast despite being admitted to hospital.

"Sonam wanted to continue the fast exactly as he had been observing it previously. He intends to continue the fast he has been maintaining. They have been urging him to consume fluids, but he refused, although he is drinking water," Angmo said.

Earlier in the day, Angmo described the Centre's concern for Wangchuk's health as a 'charade', alleging that the government feared his participation in the proposed Parliament march over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak.

"They said they brought him in because they were deeply concerned about his health, as it was declining. But these claims are incorrect. First of all, his health was not deteriorating at all. If you look at the reports from the evening prior, everything was absolutely normal; his potassium level was 4.3, and all other parameters were normal too," she said.

She claimed Wangchuk's health had not deteriorated before he was taken to Safdarjung Hospital and alleged that authorities could have informed the family before shifting him.

"If you were truly so concerned about his health, why did you send police personnel in plain clothes? Why did you so ruthlessly pick him up, put him on a stretcher, and take him away? You could have simply come to conduct a medical test and informed his family. That is the proper way to handle things in a democracy," she said.

Reiterating her allegation, Angmo said, "If you were genuinely concerned about his health, then this whole narrative about health concerns is nothing but a charade.

They were simply afraid that if Sonam set out on his march, hundreds of thousands of people would join himânot just in Delhi, but across the entire countryâand they were trying to prevent that."

Angmo also alleged that Wangchuk was not being allowed to freely consult doctors of his choice and claimed the atmosphere at the hospital resembled the conditions during his detention in Jodhpur Jail following his arrest during the 2025 Ladakh protests.

"He is not being allowed to meet his doctors. We want to consult our doctors, whom we are comfortable with. The police are constantly surveilling. When I am in the room with him, a constable accompanies me. The environment is similar to Jodhpur Jail. I was not allowed to carry my phone, and Sonam was not handed over his tablet. When we asked for orders, the police personnel had no written orders," she alleged.

The Delhi high court, however, refused to order Wangchuk's transfer from Safdarjung Hospital, observing that the material placed before it did not indicate he was under illegal detention.

The court noted that his wife, brother and other family members had unrestricted access to him and had been provided accommodation at the hospital.

The court also referred to the earlier order directing daily medical monitoring and recorded the Centre's submission that Wangchuk had been shifted to the government hospital because of his deteriorating medical condition.

According to the medical opinion placed before the court, his sugar and sodium levels were below normal and his potassium level had fallen to a dangerously low level.

The court noted that intravenous fluids had not been administered as Wangchuk had not consented to the treatment.

Security intensifies ahead of CJP's 'Chalo Sansad' march

Meanwhile, security has been intensified across the New Delhi district ahead of the Monsoon Session of Parliament and the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) proposed 'Chalo Sansad' march on Monday.

In a statement, Delhi Police said no permission had been sought or granted for any march to Parliament by the CJP.

It also said prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), formerly Section 144 of the CrPC, are in force across the New Delhi district.

The police said protest marches, processions, demonstrations and assemblies of five or more persons are prohibited, except at the designated protest site at Jantar Mantar with prior permission.

"As Parliament session is commencing from 20 July, strict security arrangements are in place to ensure public safety, security of protectees, and the protection of vital government installations," the statement read.

The police warned that anyone violating the prohibitory orders would be liable for prosecution under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and other applicable provisions of law.

Delhi Police also appealed to the public to respect the law, avoid participating in any unauthorised gathering or march and cooperate in maintaining public peace, safety and security.

World.title: FIFA World Cup Final: Spain beats Argentina 1-0 to win second title
World.content:
Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute to lift Spain to their second World Cup title with a ​1-0 win over gutsy, 10-man Argentina in Sunday’s (July 20, 2026) final.

Also read: Spain vs Argentina, FIFA World Cup final highlights

Torres’ deserved winner came ‌16 years and eight days after Andres Iniesta ​also scored in extra time to lift the Spaniards ⁠to their first World Championship with a 1-0 victory over the Netherlands.

It came on La Roja’s 20th shot of the contest against the defending ‌champions, who failed to manage any to that point and struggled to wrest possession away from their superior Iberian opponents.

That ‌was true at even strength and became more difficult ‌when ⁠the Albiceleste’s numbers were reduced when Enzo Fernandez’s late ⁠challenge of Pau Cubarsi left referee Slavko Vincic no choice but to produce a second caution just before the end of normal time.

Spain remain the only nation ​ever to win the European ‌Championship and World Cup in successive tournaments, having now done so a second time. They are also the first World Cup champion ever to concede only once across an entire tournament.

Lionel Messi’s ‌Argentina failed to earn a title for the first ​time in three major tournaments, having also captured the 2021 and 2024 Copa Americas on either side of their ⁠2022 World Cup triumph.

The 39-year-old, eight-time Ballon d’Or winner Messi finished the competition with eight goals and four assists, but had little ‌time on the ball until Spain finally took the lead and never seriously looked like lifting his side to another great moment as he has so many times in the last two World Cup cycles.

Emi Martinez made 11 saves for the Albiceleste, who fell short in their bid to be the first consecutive ‌World Cup champions since Brazil won the 1958 and 1962 titles.

What had felt ​so difficult for the first 105 minutes suddenly looked easy after 37 seconds of play in the second ⁠period of extra time.

Pedro Porro curled in an outswinging cross from ⁠the left to the back post. Nico Williams won the header and nodded it back into space, and Torres hammered ‌a half-volley at last past the flailing Martinez. It was his only goal of the tournament, making him the seventh ​player to score during a tournament in which his side never trailed.

World.title: Self-help groups to make two lakh national flags ahead of I-Day
World.content:
The Delhi government is preparing to roll out the Har Ghar Tiranga 2026 campaign ahead of Independence Day to promote public participation, patriotism and national unity. Self-Help Groups (SHGs) across Delhi have been given an important role in the campaign, and around two lakh national flags will be produced through eligible SHGs, as per the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO).

It will be organised by the State Urban Livelihood Mission (SULM) of the Delhi Government. The SULM works to strengthen the livelihoods of the urban poor by promoting Self-Help Groups and creating opportunities for skill development, entrepreneurship and self-employment.

Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said that the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign is not just about hoisting the national flag, but also an opportunity to strengthen the spirit of patriotism, national unity and public participation. She said the Delhi government is committed to making the campaign a success through the involvement of every section of society while also creating opportunities for the economic empowerment of Self-Help Groups.

The CM said the decision to involve SHGs in the production of national flags reflects the government’s approach of linking public welfare initiatives with livelihood opportunities. She said members of the Self-Help Groups producing the national flag will directly contribute to the making of the Tricolour, a symbol of the nation’s pride and national unity. Along with earning an income, they will also have the honour of being part of a nationwide campaign.

“As part of this effort, more than 15 lakh national flags will be distributed across Delhi. The government will also procure national flags from online marketplaces. The government’s effort is to ensure that the spirit of the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign reaches every household in Delhi,” Ms. Gupta said.

World.title: Maharashtra panel to study ST benefits after Christian conversion allegations
World.content:
The State government has formed a 27-member committee of legislators from Scheduled Tribes to examine the legal framework for benefits available to ST individuals after religious conversion. The move follows allegations raised in the Assembly regarding Christian missionaries in Nandurbar district’s Navapur taluka.

The decision originates from an attention notice (No. 1773) moved by Anupbhaiyya Agrawal and other members during the 2025 monsoon session of the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly. The notice stated that Christian religious leaders, missionaries, and their institutions in Navapur taluka were using inducements to compel tribals and non-tribals to convert.

During the debate on the notice, members demanded that concessions available to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes be withdrawn after conversion. The Revenue Minister and the Tribal Development Minister assured the House that a committee of ST legislators would deliberate on the matter and formulate a policy.

The 2011 Census data for Maharashtra shows that the ST population increased from 85.77 lakh in 2001 to over 1.05 crore. Among STs, 97.2% identified as Hindu. The Census recorded 1.13 lakh Muslims, over 20,000 Christians, nearly 21,000 Buddhists, and smaller numbers of Sikhs and Jains within the ST category.

Between 2001 and 2011, the Muslim ST population grew by 49.1%, Buddhist STs by 114.8%, and Jain STs by nearly six times. The Christian ST population in the state declined by 34.8% during the same decade.

The committee will be chaired by Mr. Uike. It includes the Minister of State for Tribal Development Mr. Indranil Naik; the Food and Drug Administration Minister, Mr. Narbhari Zirwal; MLAs representing ST constituencies; and the Commissioner of the Tribal Research and Training Institute (TRTI), Pune, as member secretary. The panel comprises 26 MLAs, including Mr. Amashya Padvi, Mr. Rajesh Padvi, and Dr. Vijaykumar Gavit.

The panel will study the laws of the Central government and other states concerning concessions available to ST individuals post-conversion. The state government has issued a Government Resolution through the Tribal Development Department to formalise the committee’s constitution. The panel will recommend a comprehensive policy for Maharashtra.

World.title: Government issues a show-cause notice to Janakpuri private school, proposes takeover
World.content:
The Delhi government has issued a show-cause notice to a private school in Janakpuri proposing to take over the school, over lapses including “cover-up” of sexual assault on a nursery student, Education Minister Ashish Sood said on Sunday (July 19, 2026).

“In light of these continuous and systemic failures, the Directorate of Education has asked the school’s managing Trust to explain why the government should not execute the following actions: Government Takeover: Immediate takeover of the school’s management by the Delhi Government under Section 20(1) of the Delhi School Education Act (DSEA), 1973,” an official statement from the Minister’s office.

A three-year-old girl was raped allegedly by a 57-year-old caretaker on the school premises on April 30.

The Minister said that the government has absolute zero tolerance for any compromise on the safety and dignity of our children. “A school stands in loco parentis, it is legally and morally responsible for every child on its premises. If an institution covers up a heinous crime like child abuse, operates illegal branches in residential basements, and loots public funds, we will not sit quietly. We are prepared to completely take over the management and recommend the cancellation of their land lease,” Mr. Sood said.

The school management “deliberately” failed to report this heinous incident to the Directorate of Education, violating mandatory child protection laws, as per the statement.

“When the police visited the pre-primary branch to investigate the crime, all 64 CCTV cameras installed on the premises were found to be completely non-functional. The school had intentionally operated without a maintenance contract,” the statement said.

The school was “illegally” operating its nursery and KG classes from a private residential building in Narang Colony without any authorisation and the basement of this unauthorized building was being used as an unsupervised activity area for minor children, as per the Minister’s office.

“The school had no Child Protection Policy, no Child Protection Committee, and no POCSO-trained Nodal Officer. Essential security staff, including guards, had not undergone mandatory police background verification,” the statement said.

The management allegedly diverted approximately ₹6 crores meant for staff retirement benefits to another branch under the guise of “loan settlement”, and they also paid unauthorised professional fees to the school’s manager and trustees out of the school fund, as per the official statement.

World.title: Srinagar’s Vichar Nag temple sees puja again, L-G says ‘revival serves as a historic bridge’
World.content:
A ‘Pran Pratishtha’ ceremony was held at the historic Vichar Nag Temple in Srinagar on Sunday (July 20, 2026), once a hub of militancy.

Scores of Kashmiri Pandits attended the ceremony in an area that once hosted a number of Pandit families who had to leave their homeland due to militancy in the 1990s.

Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha visited the shrine and took stock of the renovation works.

“For millennia, this sacred temple has anchored India’s spiritual, intellectual, and philosophical journey. Its revival serves as a historic bridge, connecting our past, present, and future. It marks the return of a consciousness that, for centuries, nurtured an unbroken tradition of reflection, dialogue, and learning. Restoring Vichar Nag is a vital step toward preserving the rich, diverse cultural heritage of Jammu Kashmir,” Mr. Sinha said.

‘Vibrant hub of knowledge’

He said Vichar Nag holds a sacred place in the cultural and spiritual heritage of Jammu and Kashmir. “The revival of this historic site, once a vibrant hub of knowledge where scholars from across the globe gathered for intellectual discourse, is deeply gratifying,” Mr. Sinha said.

After a long hiatus, devotees gathered at the shrine to perform yajna and havan.

The Lieutenant-Governor was accompanied by Rajiv Pandey, Deputy Inspector General; Akshay Labroo, Deputy Commissioner, Srinagar; and Dr. G.V. Sundeep Chakravarthy, Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Srinagar.

The Vishwa Kashmiri Samaj (VKS), a Pandit body, praised the restoration and development work at the temple complex.

World.title: Maharashtra govt allows hotels, restaurants, bars to remain open till 4 a.m. for FIFA World Cup final
World.content:
The Maharashtra government has permitted licensed hotels, restaurants and bars across the State to remain open till 4 a.m. on Monday to facilitate screening of the FIFA World Cup final between Argentina and Spain, according to an official order.

The Home Department issued the directive on Saturday (July 18) following a request from the National Restaurant Association of India (NRAI), Mumbai, which sought extension of operating hours for hospitality establishments on the night of the final.

The order, issued under Maharashtra Police Act, said the relaxation would be applicable only for the FIFA World Cup final and only to licensed hotels, restaurants and bars.

The government directed establishments to deploy adequate private security personnel to prevent traffic congestion and maintain law and order in and around their premises.

It warned that any untoward incident or violation of law would attract action against the establishment under the relevant legal provisions.

The order also asked establishments to comply with all licence conditions and directions issued by the Excise Department and local authorities. It clarified that the extended timings would not apply to any establishments other than licensed hotels, restaurants and bars.

District administrations and police have been directed to ensure strict implementation of the order, while all establishments have been instructed to cease operations immediately after 4 a.m..

World.title: West Asia war LIVE: Iranian missile hits Jordan's Aqaba Airport, reports Iran state media
World.content:
According to Israeli media, an Iranian missile hit Jordan’s Aqaba Airport, with the impact visible from Eilat, Israel.

The Israeli military said Sunday (July 19, 2026) it had identified missiles launched from Iran towards Aqaba in Jordan, after Jordan’s government denied the city’s airport and seaport were evacuated over a threat.

“A short while ago, the IDF identified the launch of missiles from Iran toward the city of Aqaba in Jordan, adjacent to Israeli territory,” the military said. “It is possible that as a result of the fire, there will be spillover into Israeli territory.”

The U.S. military said on Sunday (July 19, 2026) that it launched new airstrikes against Iran to “swiftly punish” the country’s Revolutionary Guard for an attack in Jordan that killed two American service members, left one missing and four requiring hospitalisation.

The strikes were designed to further degrade Iran’s ability to restrict the traffic of oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, U.S. Central Command said.

World.title: Torres’ strike helps Spain defeat Argentina 1-0, lift second World Cup trophy
World.content:
The name of Ferran Torres will be etched in Spanish football history as the Barcelona player struck in the second half of Extra Time to help Spain defeat Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final on Sunday. This was Spain’s second World Cup title with the first one coming back in 2010 when they defeated Netherlands 1-0 in the final.

The match had ended goal-less after 90 mins which necessitated Extra Time. Argentina were down to 10 men after Enzo Fernandez was sent off in second-half stoppage time after getting his second yellow card. Fernandez was carded for a reckless play that sent Spain defender Pau Cubarsi cartwheeling into the air, and the card came out immediately.

Another foul about two minutes after play resumed gave Lamine Yamal a chance to win it from about 22 yards out on a free kick. Yamal’s strike was curling toward the right post, and Martinez dived to knock it away for his 10th save of the afternoon — the most ever in a World Cup final.

He leaped to his feet, punching the air and imploring the crowd to get loud. Not long after that came the whistle, sending the game to extra time.

Spain took 15 shots in regulation, Argentina none. Spain took nine corners, Argentina one. And somehow, 90-plus minutes of that sort of dominance wasn’t enough.



It was the ninth 0-0 score at halftime in the 23 World Cup finals, including the 1950 Uruguay-Brazil match that wasn’t an actual final but decided the champion.

Argentina made three changes from its starting 11 for the semifinal win over England: Midfielders Rodrigo De Paul and Nico Gonzalez, along with defender Gonzalo Montiel were in, while midfielders Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina, along with forward Giuliano Simeone, were dropped.

Spain kept its starting 11 from the semifinal win over France untouched. It was the 104th and last match of the biggest World Cup ever, a 48-team event that played out over the US, Canada and Mexico.

Because there were more matches than any previous World Cup, it was no surprise that there were more goals than all other editions – 307 and counting entering Sunday.



Post Malone headlined the closing ceremony, which started about 90 minutes before the final was set to begin and just a few minutes after Messi and Argentina arrived at the stadium.

President Donald Trump was present as well, with plans calling for him to be part of the trophy presentation at the conclusion of the match.

“I won’t pick sides,” Trump told Fox Sports in an interview released Sunday afternoon before the final. “I just think it’s very hard to bet against Messi. He’s great.” Argentina was wearing its light blue and white vertically striped jerseys for the match, while Spain was wearing predominantly red with navy sleeves. The officiating crew was from Slovenia – Slavko Vincic is the referee, with Tomaz Klancnik and Andraz Kovacic his assistant referees.

World.title: 0 shots in 90 mins: Argentina’s unwanted record vs Spain in World Cup final
World.content:
Argentina became the first side to fail to register a single shot in 90 minutes in a FIFA World Cup final when they were utterly dominated by Spain on Sunday. However, they still defended resolutely, taking the match to Extra Time.

Argentina’s task was made even tougher when Enzo Fernandez was sent off in the second-half stoppage time after getting his second yellow card, meaning Argentina was down to 10 players. Fernandez was carded for a reckless play that sent Spain defender Pau Cubarsi cartwheeling into the air, and the card came out immediately.



Spain took 15 shots in regulation, Argentina none. Spain took nine corners, Argentina one. And somehow, 90-plus minutes of that sort of dominance wasn’t enough.

World.title: Shubman Gill on Rohit Sharma’s future: He has not told us anything
World.content:
India captain Shubman Gill has said there hasn’t been any discussion with Rohit Sharma about the Lord’s ODI being his last for international appearance. With an eye on the 2027 World Cup, as reported by The Indian Express, the selectors have informed the 39-year-old Rohit that the England series will be his last.



However, there hasn’t been any official word from Rohit or from the selectors so far. Having played two subdued knocks in the first two ODIs, on Sunday Rohit scored 138 in a losing cause. Despite scoring a century, it wasn’t the former India captain who turned up for the post-match media conference, where skipper Shubman Gill showed up.

World.title: Bloodshed in Balochistan: Why Pakistan’s resource-rich province remains in conflict
World.content:
For 10 days in Pakistan recently, family members of 27 policemen killed in Balochistan sat on a protest, refusing to bury their dead till the government accepted their demands. Last week, their sit-in ended after the authorities agreed to set up a judicial commission to investigate two recent attacks — in Ziarat on July 6, in which the policemen were killed, and in Hanna Urak a day before, in which five civilians were killed — allegedly by Baloch militants.

‘Operation Shaban’ was also launched in response to the killing of the policemen, in which 129 “terrorists” have been killed since July 5, Pakistani authorities claim.

This is the latest in a long history of bloodshed, militancy, and state repression in Balochistan, where Pakistan accuses India of fomenting trouble. Bordering Iran and Afghanistan, Balochistan is not just strategically important for Pakistan, but is also its richest state in terms of natural resources. Why, then, does conflict continue to simmer here? We explain, in five points.

Partition roots of Balochistan problem

When the British left the Indian subcontinent in 1947, the princely states were given the option of joining either India or the newly created Pakistan. The present-day Balochistan was then a collection of tribal principalities. Like many other parts of the world, the British empire had divided the Baloch areas arbitrarily, transferring some to the control of the Persian empire.

In 1947, the main tribal principality here was of Kalat. The Khan of Kalat, Mir Ahmad Yar Khan, wished to remain independent. However, as the months rolled on, pressure started increasing on him to join Pakistan, as the other tribal feudatories around Kalat all acceded. Isolated and facing Pakistani military pressure, the Khan finally acceded on March 27, 1948. The disagreement over Kalat’s accession became one of the foundational grievances for Baloch nationalists, although Pakistan considers the accession final and legal.



In almost every decade of Pakistan’s life, it has faced insurgency in Balochistan. The current one, which began under Pervez Musharraf, is believed to be the fifth, triggered by the 2005 rape of a Baloch doctor by an army officer at her home on the Sui gas plant, and then the killing in 2006 of powerful local leader Akbar Bugti.

Tussle over ethnic differences, natural resources

The Baloch are an ethnically distinct community. In fact, all of Pakistan’s provinces, from Sindh to Balochistan to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to Punjab, have distinct identities, and all three have complained, to varying degrees, of Punjabi domination.

Balochistan is rich in reserves of copper, gold, natural gas, etc. However, it is sparsely populated, and the Baloch people say they have not been allowed to reap the fruits of their state’s natural wealth.



Some of Pakistan’s show-piece foreign projects are in Balochsitan. China has built invested heavily in the strategic Gwadar port, the crown jewel of the China Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC). The Saindak copper and gold mine is run by China. Last December, the Donald Trump administration announced it would invest $1.3 billion in the Reko Diq copper and gold mine.

Gwadar port on the Arabian Sea, close to the Strait of Hormuz, is in Balochistan. (Photo: Wikimedia Commons) Gwadar port on the Arabian Sea, close to the Strait of Hormuz, is in Balochistan. (Photo: Wikimedia Commons)

The Baloch people have opposed the exploitation of their land to fill foreign pockets, and pointed out that even the plum jobs of engineers and managers often go to Punjabis or Sindhis. China-funded projects, and Chinese workers, have been major targets of Baloch militants.



However, Pakistan government dismisses the claims of widespread discontent in Balochistan. Ali Chishti, a defence and security expert from Pakistan, told The Indian Express, “Millions of Baloch participate in the country’s political, economic, and military institutions. The insurgency represents a small militant movement, not the will of the Baloch people. Pakistan has consistently maintained that these militant groups receive support from India, an allegation India rejects. Attempts to portray Balochistan as evidence of a failed state ignore both the facts on the ground and the continued commitment of the Pakistani state to the province’s security, development, and prosperity.”

Baloch people’s demands

The Baloch insurgency in no way speaks in one voice. There is a section that wants an independent state of Balochistan and restores to violence for its aims. But there are many others who are happy to work within the constitutional framework in Pakistan, demanding greater autonomy and greater control over decisions that affect their region.



The discontent has evolved over the years. While there is a middle class that speaks the language of activism, petitions, and political representation, the violent organisations, such as the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), have gained in strength. They primarily target State or Army-linked places and people, but have also killed civilians.

Then there is the fact that in Pakistan, militants and terrorists are highly trained and have access to sophisticated weaponry, because of the NATO war against terror in Afghanistan. After the Americans withdrew from Afghanistan in 2021, they left behind large quantities of advanced weapons and battle-hardened fighters.

In the past couple of years, since the Taliban came back to power in Kabul, Pakistani security forces have claimed there are signs of collaboration between the BLA and the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), or the Pakistan Taliban.



The ‘disappeared’ people of Balochistan

A major, and very emotive, issue in Balochistan is that of disappearing people. Activists allege that over the years, some 5,000 people, picked up by security forces, have either never been found or found dead months or even years later. Last month, Maharang Baloch, a prominent activist working on the issue of disappearances, was sentenced to life imprisonment.

The state claims these ‘disappeared’ people have either joined the militancy or have left home on their own accord.

The State’s response

The Pakistan government’s response in Balochistan has usually been heavy handed, with Operation Shaban being the continuation of a long trend. Voices within Pakistan have pointed out that an insurgency that has local support cannot be rooted out through force alone.



When asked if the government was planning a political process parallel to Operation Shaban, Chishti said, “The State is always talking, but would not with foreign sponsored proxies or terrorists.”
